And the conjecture of Seder HaDorot is that this is not the Tanna R' Shimon bar Kahana, but another man of this name, and therefore he divided him into two; however, I do not know why he divided him into two, and on the contrary, from there it is implied that the Shimon bar Kahana who was killed is the disciple of R' Eliezer, as is known that R' Eliezer's place of residence was in Lod, and so too his disciple resided there and was killed there; and this requires further study.

div.head: R' Shimon bar Karsana.
div.ab: נזכר אך בירושלמי והיה תלמידו דר׳ אחא שאמר תמיד בשמו כשבת פ״א רה״ח, עירובין פ״א ה״ז (פ״ג סה"ד, וברי״ף ספ״א דעירובין גורס ר"ש בר ביסנא), יומא פ״ג ה״ח, ביצה פ״ה ה״ח, ע״ז רפ״א.

He is mentioned only in the Yerushalmi, and he was the disciple of R' Aḥa, for he always spoke in his name, as in Yerushalmi Shabbat 1, start of halakhah 8, Yerushalmi Eruvin 1:7 (3, end of halakhah 4, and in the Rif at the end of chapter 1 of Eruvin he reads R' Shimon bar Bisna), Yerushalmi Yoma 3:8, Yerushalmi Beitzah 5:8, Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah, start of chapter 1.
ומצינו ע״ז פ״א ה״א ר״ש בר ברסנא בשם ר' אחא וצ״ל בר כרסנא.
And we find in Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah 1:1: "R' Shimon bar Barsana in the name of R' Aḥa," and one must read "bar Karsana."
ונשתבש יותר בדמאי פ״ג סה״א ושם ר' שמעון בר סני בשם ר׳ אחא וצ״ל בר כרסנא, והטעות בא שהיה כתוב בר כרסני ונשמט חד בר ותיבת כרסני נחלק לשתים ומכ״ף נעשה בי״ת.

And it became even more corrupted in Yerushalmi Demai 3, end of halakhah 1, and there [it reads]: "R' Shimon bar Sani in the name of R' Aḥa," and one must read "bar Karsana"; and the error came about because it was written "bar Karsani," and one "bar" was omitted, and the word "Karsani" was split into two, and out of the kaf a bet was made.
ונזכר תרומות פ״ב ה״ג, מעשרות פ״א ה״ב, חלה פ״ד סה״ג, שבת רפ״ג.
And he is mentioned in Yerushalmi Terumot 2:3, Yerushalmi Maaserot 1:2, Yerushalmi Ḥallah 4, end of halakhah 3, Yerushalmi Shabbat, start of chapter 3.
ומצינו שבת רפ״א־ב: ר׳ אלעזר בשם ר״ש כרסנא ונראה שצ״ל ר״א בר׳ יוסי בשם ר״ש בר כרסנא, והוא ר׳ אלעזר ב״ר יוסי האחרון.

And we find in Yerushalmi Shabbat, start of chapter 1:2: "R' Elazar in the name of R' Shimon Karsana," and it appears that one must read "R' Elazar bar R' Yose in the name of R' Shimon bar Karsana," and he is the later R' Elazar bar R' Yose.

div.head: R' Shimon ben Levi.
div.ab: ‫נזכר קידושין מ ‪ , :‬אבל המאמר מיבא‬ ‫סוכה נב‪ .‬ושם ר״ש בן לקיש‪,‬‬ ‫ובחולין נז: (לגרסת דק"ס) שאל ר' יוסי בן נהוראי את ר״ש בן לוי.

The Hebrew of this paragraph on Wikisource is uncorrected OCR (columns mixed, letters confused). The translation is not reliable; read the scan. He is mentioned in Kiddushin 40b, but the statement is brought in Sukkah 52a, and there [it reads] R' Shimon ben Lakish; and in Ḥullin 57b (according to the version of Dikdukei Soferim) R' Yosi ben Nehorai asked R' Shimon ben Levi.
וכן נזכר תנחומא בהר־ז, ויק״ר פט״ז־ז,
And likewise he is mentioned in Tanḥuma Behar 7, Vayikra Rabbah 16:7,

‫ומדי שמואל פי״ח־ד מאמרו היק״ כל‬ ‫שהוא רחמן על אכזרים סוף שהוא נעשה‬ ‫אכזר על רחמנים (כצ"ל), ‬ובילקוט שם‬ ‫מובא המאמר ע״ש ריב״ל‪.‬‬ ‫ובילקוט ישעיה רמז שלו ר׳ אבא בשם‬ ‫ר״ש בן לוי ובילקוט שהש״ר רמז תתקפ״ח‬ ‫ר׳ תחליפא דקסרין בש״ר שטעון בן לוי‪,‬‬ ‫וצ״ל בבשהש״ר פ״ד פ׳ נפת בשם ר'‬ ‫שמעון בן לקיש.

The translation is not reliable; read the scan. and Midrash Shmuel 18:4 [brings] his precious statement: "Whoever is merciful to the cruel, in the end becomes cruel to the merciful" (so one must read), and in the Yalkut there the statement is brought in the name of R' Yehoshua ben Levi. And in Yalkut Isaiah remez 336 [it reads] R' Abba in the name of R' Shimon ben Levi, and in Yalkut Shir HaShirim Rabbah remez 988 [it reads] R' Taḥlifa of Caesarea in the name of R' Shimon ben Levi, and one must read as in Shir HaShirim Rabbah chapter 4, on the verse "Your lips drip flowing honey" [Song of Songs 4:11], in the name of R' Shimon ben Lakish.

div.head: R' Shimon ben Lakish - Resh Lakish.
div.ab: ‫ע״פ רוב נקרא בבבלי בשם ריש לקיש‪,‬‬ ‫ובירושלמי בשם ר״ש בן לקיש ואך‬ ‫בסנהדרין נקרא בכמה מקומות בשם ריש‬ ‫לקיש ועור באיזה מקומות‪.‬‬ ‫בדבר הנחל בענקים הזה אשר עליי‬ ‫אטרויוטא ט ‪ :‬מאן דמשתעי ר״לבהדיה‬ ‫בשוקאיהבו ליה עסקא בלא םהדי‪ ,‬באה‬ ‫ערבוביא נחלה יש שרוצים לומר ששני‬ ‫ר״ל הוי כדמובא בתורה מציון ש׳יד‬ ‫חוברת ד׳ כח‪ .‬מאת החכם ‪ ,‬ר״ש דוד‬ ‫שאחר היה בן דורו דרכינו הקדוש ואפשר‬ ‫שהיה עוד קשיש טובא מרבי והשני ניסו י‬ ‫דרי יוחנן‪ ,‬וכבר אמר החכם כדי לתקן‬ ‫י שניאה 'אחת צריכין אנו לעשית שניאית‬ ‫רבות‪ ,‬אבל כל דבריו ישא רוח‪ ,‬וקישייתו‬ ‫מב״ר פע״ח שבשעת הליו של רבי הלך‬ ‫ר״ל למשאל בשלומו ורבי בקשו שיתפלל‬ ‫עליו‪ ,‬וכן שם רפ״פ שיוסי מעונאה פגע‬ ‫בכבוד הנשיא הוא רבי אשר היטב חרה‬ ‫לו וברמשא הלך ר״ל לפייס את רבי‪,‬‬ ‫במחילה טעה טעות נ ח ל שחשב שזה‬ ‫רבי רבינו הקדוש ולא ידע שכל הנשיאים‬ ‫היו נקראין בירושלמי ובמדרשים )שהעתיקו‬ ‫ע"‪ 1‬רוב דבריהם מירושלמי( בשם רבי‪ ,‬ורבי‬ ‫זה שבקש לר״ל שיתפלל עליו הוא נכד‬ ‫נכדו של רבי היינו ר״י נשיאה השני‬ ‫אשד נם ר׳׳ל יעצמו לא היה מתחלה‬ ‫מאוהביו כמביאר בערכו‪ ,‬ואח״כ היה‬ ‫מאוהביו הנאמנים‪ ,‬ולפי דעתי אין ראוי‬ ‫יותר לטפל בדבריו שאין להם שום יסוד.

The Hebrew of this paragraph on Wikisource is uncorrected OCR (columns mixed, letters confused). The translation is not reliable; read the scan. For the most part he is called in the Bavli by the name Resh Lakish, and in the Yerushalmi by the name R' Shimon ben Lakish, though in [Yerushalmi] Sanhedrin he is called in several places by the name Resh Lakish, and also in a few other places. Regarding this great man among giants, of whom it was said in Yoma 9b, "Anyone with whom Resh Lakish conversed in the marketplace, they would give him merchandise [on credit] without witnesses," a great confusion has arisen. There are those who wish to say that there were two Resh Lakishes, as brought in Torah MiTzion, Year 4, Booklet 4, page 28a, by the scholar R' S. David: that one was a contemporary of Rabbenu ha-Kadosh, and perhaps was even much older than Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], and the second was the brother-in-law of R' Yoḥanan. The sage already said, "In order to correct one error, we must commit many errors"; however, the wind shall carry away all his words. His difficulty from Bereishit Rabbah 78, that at the time of Rabbi's illness Resh Lakish went to inquire after his welfare and Rabbi requested of him to pray for him, and likewise there at the beginning of chapter 80, that Yosi of Ma'on slighted the honor of the Nasi, who is Rabbi, who was very angry, and in the evening Resh Lakish went to appease Rabbi—with all due respect, he made a great mistake in thinking that this "Rabbi" is Rabbenu ha-Kadosh, and did not know that all the Nesi'im were called in the Yerushalmi and in the midrashim (which copied the majority of their words from the Yerushalmi) by the name "Rabbi." And this "Rabbi" who requested of Resh Lakish to pray for him is the grandson of the grandson of Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi], namely R' Yehuda Nesi'ah the Second, of whom Resh Lakish himself was at first not among his friends, as is explained in his entry, and afterward became one of his faithful friends. In my opinion, it is not worthwhile to deal any further with his words, as they have no foundation whatsoever.

ויש שרוצים לומר שהיה עוד קודם בן עזאי ע״פ מה שמובא בפדר״א פמ״ג שאמר בן עזאי בא וראה כח התשובה מרשב״ל שהיה הוא ושני רעיו גוזלים וחומסים — והוא שב בתשובה — והיה עוסק בתורה כל ימיו — וביום שמת מתו שני רעיו השודדים ונתנו לרשב״ל חלק החיים ולשני רעיו בשאול תחתיות, אבל כבר העיר בצדק הגאון רד״ל בפירושו על הפדר״א שט"ס נפל בספרים בשם בן עזאי.

And there are those who wish to say that he lived even before Ben Azzai, based on what is brought in Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, chapter 43, that Ben Azzai said: "Come and see the power of repentance from R' Shimon ben Lakish, for he and his two companions were robbers and brigands—and he repented—and he engaged in Torah all his days—and on the day he died, his two robber companions died, and they gave to R' Shimon ben Lakish a portion in life, and to his two companions in the lowest netherworld." However, the Gaon R' David Luria, in his commentary on Pirkei de-Rabbi Eliezer, has already rightly pointed out that a scribal error fell into the texts regarding the name of Ben Azzai.
אבל האמת הברור שאך ורק הד ר׳ שמעון בן לקיש הוה וכאשר נבאר.
However, the clear truth is that there was one and only one R' Shimon ben Lakish, as we shall explain.

השם לקיש אם הוא שם אביו או שהוא שם עיר כדעת הרב ראה״וו כבית תלמוד שנה ג' לא נודע לנו, יען שלא נמצא בשום מקום עיר בשם לקיש, ומה שקיצרו את שמו וקראוהו בשם ריש לקיש כבר העיר ע״ז הגאון ר״י פיק ודעתו שהוא באשמת המדפיסים הראשונים נשתנה מרשב״ל לריש לקיש, וקשה לומר כן ולשבש בכל המקומות שנקרא בשם ר״ל, וכן מובא בדק״ס בכל הכ״י כמה פעמים בשם ריש לקיש, אבל טעם האמיתי נעלם ממנו למה קצרו שמו, ואך זאת ידוע לנו שקרא את עצמו בשם ״בר לקישא״ במגילה כח: וכן קראו ר׳ יוחנן כב״מ פד.

Whether the name Lakish is the name of his father or the name of a city, as is the opinion of Rabbi R. A. H. Weiss in Beit Talmud, Year 3, is unknown to us, since a city by the name of Lakish is not found anywhere. And as for why they shortened his name and called him by the name Resh Lakish, the Gaon R' Yeshayah Pik already remarked on this, and his opinion is that due to the fault of the early printers it was changed from R' Shimon ben Lakish to Resh Lakish. Yet it is difficult to say so and to declare every place where he is called by the name Resh Lakish to be an error; and likewise in Dikdukei Soferim he is brought in all the manuscripts several times by the name Resh Lakish. However, the true reason why they shortened his name is hidden from us; only this is known to us, that he called himself by the name "Bar Lakisha" in Megillah 28b, and so R' Yoḥanan called him in Bava Metzia 84a.
אבותיו ידוע לנו שהיו מגדולי הדור כשבת קיט: שא״ל ר״ל לר' יהודה נשיאה ב) ״כך מקובלני מאבותי״ ואמרי לה מאבותיך כל עיר שאין בה תינוקות של בית רבן מחריבין אותה.

It is known to us that his ancestors were among the great men of the generation, as in Shabbat 119b, where Resh Lakish said to R' Yehuda Nesi'ah [II]: "Thus I have a tradition from my ancestors"—and some say, "from your ancestors"—"that any city in which there are no school-children, they destroy it."

והנה דעת ר״ת בתוס׳ ב״מ פד‪ .‬ד״ה‬ ‫אי הדרת‪ ,‬שמתחלה היה ר״ל תלמיד‬ ‫חכם ואח״כ פרק מעליו עול תורה ונעשה‬ ‫ע״ה‪ ,‬וכן כתבו עירובין םהז שר״ל היה‬ ‫גברא רבה מקורם‪ ,‬ובמחילה מעצמותיהם‬ ‫הקדושים‪ ,‬איך אפשר לומר‪ ,‬על קדוש‬ ‫ישראל כן‪ ,‬ועוד ממקום שהביאו ראיה‬

The Hebrew of this paragraph on Wikisource is uncorrected OCR (columns mixed, letters confused). The translation is not reliable; read the scan. Now, the opinion of Rabbenu Tam in Tosafot Bava Metzia 84a, s.v. Iy hadart, is that initially Resh Lakish was a Torah scholar, and afterward he cast off the yoke of Torah from himself and became an ignoramus; and so they wrote in Eruvin 65b that Resh Lakish was a great man beforehand. With all due forgiveness from their holy bones, how is it possible to say such a thing about a holy one of Israel? Furthermore, from the very place that they brought proof

‫לדבריהם משם מוכח ממש להיפוך שאסרו‬ ‫שם ב״מ פד‪ ,‬אקדייה ואתנייה‪ ,‬איך‬ ‫אפשר לומר שאם היה מקודם גברא‬ ‫רבה שישכח גס לקרות בתודה או גם‬ ‫לשבח הא״ב? ומעירובין סה‪. :‬שאמרו‬ ‫ר״ל ותלמידי דר׳ חגיגא איקלעו — א״ל‬ ‫ר״ל גשבור ולכשנניע אצל רבותיגו‬ ‫שבדרום גשאל להם אתו שיילו לר' אפס‪,‬‬ ‫ואמרו שם בתים׳ שרי אפם חי אחר רבי‬ ‫אך ב׳ שגיס ומחצה אם כן תיכף אחר‬ ‫פטירת דבי היה כבר ר״ל גדול הדור‪,‬‬ ‫ובימי ר' חגיגא מציגו םגהדרין פ״א ה״ב‬ ‫ד' חגיגא פתח‪ ,‬ר׳ יוחגן ור״ל חתמין‪.‬‬ ‫ובן גדה םפ״ב ר׳ חגיגא הוה שרי בציפורין‬ ‫והוה ר״יור״ל שרויןתמן ולא הוה מצרף‬ ‫לו עימיה — חד זמן צרפון עימיה אמרין‬ ‫מה חמא רבי משגח עליגן ובו‪ /‬ובזמן ר׳‬ ‫יהודה נשיאה הראשון ור׳ אושעיה מציגו‬ ‫יבמות גז‪ .‬שבעי מיגיה ר׳ יוחגן מר׳‬ ‫"אושעיה ולא אמר לו ולא מידי לסוף‬ ‫אתא גברא רבה ומגו ר״ל ופשט ליה‬ ‫א״ל ר״י גשיאה לד׳ אושעיה אטו ר׳‬ ‫יוחגן לא• גברא רבה הוא ובו‪ /‬וזה היה‬ ‫עור טרם שמלך ר׳ יוחנן בטבריא והיו‬ ‫כולם בציפורי ור׳ אפס ואח״כ ר' חנינא‬ ‫היו מראשי ישיבה שם ור״ל ור״י היו‬ ‫מתלמידיהם הגדולים א״ב איך אפשר‬ ‫לעלות על הרעת לומר שפתאום יעזוב‬ ‫ר״ל דרכו ותורתו י ולדבק עם חומםץ‬ ‫וגזלגין ולשכח כל תורתו?‬ ‫אך האמת יורה דרכו שמעולם לא‬ ‫היה גברא רבה טרם שאירע המעשה עם‬ ‫ר׳ יוחנן והיה אז עיר •בעצם ימי עלומיו‬ ‫וכאשר נבאר‪.‬‬ ‫כפי הנראה נולד בציפורי מקום רבינו‬ ‫הקדוש חכה עיר לראותו כביצה פ״ה‬ ‫ה״ב ר׳ יוחנן ורשב״ל אמרי לא זכינן‬ ‫לאורייתא אלא בגין דחזינן לאצבעותיה‬ ‫דרבי מן גולגיקין דידיה‪ ,‬אבל ר׳ יוחנן‬ ‫היה קשיש מר״ל‪ ,‬כי ר״י זכה להיות‬ מתלמידיו הקטגים דרבי ושמע ממגו‬ ‫הלכות‪ ,‬אבל ד״ל היה ילד וזבד‪ ,‬אך‬ ‫לראותו‪ ,‬וזה שמציגו חולין גד‪ .‬ששאל‬ ‫ר״ל לר׳ יוחגן מגו רב ומגו רב ולא‬ ‫ידעגא ליה‪ ,‬א״ל ר׳ יוחגן ולא גהירא‬ ‫ליה לאותו תלמיד ששימש את דבי רבה‬ ‫וד״ח‪ ,‬וזה כמו שאמרנו שרי יוחנן שהיה‬ ‫בפטירת רבי לערך טו׳ שנה כמבואר‬ ‫בערכו‪ ,‬לכן ידע היטב את רב ונדולתו‬ ‫בעיני רבי‪ ,‬אבל ר״ל אף שהיה בן משפחה‬ ‫גדולה בציפורי וזבה לראות את רבי‪,‬‬ ‫אבל לא ידע את רב וגדולתו‪ ,‬ולכן לא‬ ‫מציגו בשום מקים שיאמר ר״ל בשם רבי‪,‬‬ ‫והילד הזה הוגן מאת הטבע בגמרות‬ ‫גפלאה שלא התיירא מפגי כל‪ ,‬והתחבר‬ ‫עם אגשים גבורי חיל כמותו ויהי עליהם‬ ‫לראש וגטה מן אורח הישר ולא שם לבו‬ ‫לתורה אף שאבותיו היו גדולי הדור‪,‬‬ ‫וגשאר לגו זברוגות ממעשיו בימים‬ ‫ההם טה שים־פר גיטין מז‪ .‬שזבן גפשיה‬ ‫ללודאיוםטך על גבורתו שיבער הרשעה‬ ‫מקרב הארץ את כת האוכלים בשר אדם‪,‬‬ ‫ובאשר יםיפר שם שהמית את כולם‬ ‫והיה זאת תמיד לשיחה בפיו לאמר אלו‬ ‫זנגת גפשך ללודין כירושלמי תרומות‬ ‫פ״ח ה״ג‪.‬‬ ‫וכן גם כשהיה כבר מראשי גדולי‬ ‫הדור יסופר עליו בירושלמי תרומות‬ ‫ספ״ח שר׳ אימי תפשוהו גזלגין עד שר׳‬ ‫יונתן התייאש ממגו‪ ,‬אך רשב״לאמר‬ ‫אגי ארדוף אחריהם ואהרוג אותם או אני‬ ‫אהרג‪ ,‬וסוף היה שהצילו מידם‪.‬‬ ‫וכן יסופר שם שפ״א חמסו לסטים‬ ‫מר׳ ייחגן כל ממוגו ור״ל רדף אחריהם‬ ‫יהשיגם והשיבו את כל רכושו‪.‬‬ ‫ירי ייחגן שידע היטב את ר״ל מנעוריו‬ ‫וראה אותי איך שמעט מעט הטה מן‬ ‫דרך הישר ומתחבר לרשעימ‪ ,‬השתוקק‬ ‫מאוד להחזירו למוטב‪ ,‬וכבר היה אז ר״ל‬ ‫בעצם ימי עלומיו והנה אנה ה׳ לידו

The Hebrew of this paragraph on Wikisource is uncorrected OCR (columns mixed, letters confused). The translation is not reliable; read the scan. for their words, from there the exact opposite is proven! For they said there in Bava Metzia 84a: "He taught him Scripture and taught him Mishnah." How is it possible to say that if he had previously been a great man, he would forget even how to read the Torah, or even forget the alef-bet? And from Eruvin 65b, where they said: "Resh Lakish and the disciples of R' Ḥanina happened to come [to a certain place]... Resh Lakish said to them: 'Let us rent [now], and when we reach our masters in the South we shall ask them.' They came and asked R' Efes"—and they said there in Tosafot that R' Efes lived after Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] only two and a half years; if so, immediately after the passing of Rabbi, Resh Lakish was already the great man of the generation! And in the days of R' Ḥanina we find in Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 1:2: "R' Ḥanina opened [the discourse], R' Yoḥanan and Resh Lakish concluded." And likewise in [Yerushalmi] Niddah, at the end of chapter 2: "R' Ḥanina was residing in Tzippori, and R' Yoḥanan and Resh Lakish were residing there, and he did not join them to himself... One time he joined them to himself; they said, 'What did Rabbi see to take notice of us?' etc." And in the time of R' Yehuda Nesi'ah the First and R' Oshaya, we find in Yevamot 57a that R' Yoḥanan asked a question of R' Oshaya, and he said nothing to him; "Finally a great man came—and who was it? Resh Lakish—and resolved it for him. R' Yehuda Nesi'ah said to R' Oshaya: 'Is R' Yoḥanan not a great man?' etc." And this was even before R' Yoḥanan reigned [as head of the academy] in Tiberias, and they were all in Tzippori, and R' Efes and afterward R' Ḥanina were among the heads of the yeshiva there, and Resh Lakish and R' Yoḥanan were among their great disciples. If so, how could it enter the mind to say that suddenly Resh Lakish would abandon his way and his Torah, to cleave to brigands and robbers and to forget all his Torah?
Rather, the truth shows its own way: that he was never a great man before the incident with R' Yoḥanan occurred, and he was then still in the very prime of his youth, as we shall explain.
As it appears, he was born in Tzippori, the place of Rabbenu ha-Kadosh, and still merited to see him, as in Yerushalmi Beitzah 5:2: "R' Yoḥanan and R' Shimon ben Lakish said: 'We did not merit Torah except because we saw the fingers of Rabbi [protruding] from his boots.'" However, R' Yoḥanan was older than Resh Lakish, for R' Yoḥanan merited to be among the youngest disciples of Rabbi and heard halakhot from him, whereas Resh Lakish was a child and merited only to see him. And this is what we find in Ḥullin 54a, where Resh Lakish asked R' Yoḥanan: "'Who is Rav, and who is Rav, that I do not know him?' R' Yoḥanan said to him: 'Do you not remember that disciple who attended upon Rabbi the Great and R' Ḥiyya?'" And this is as we have said: that R' Yoḥanan, who at the passing of Rabbi was about fifteen years old, as is explained in his entry, therefore knew Rav and his greatness in the eyes of Rabbi well; whereas Resh Lakish, although he was the son of a great family in Tzippori and merited to see Rabbi, nevertheless did not know Rav and his greatness. And therefore we do not find in any place that Resh Lakish says [a teaching] in the name of Rabbi.
And this child was endowed by nature with wondrous strength, so that he was not afraid of anyone, and he joined with men of valor like himself and became a leader over them, and strayed from the straight path and did not set his heart on the Torah, even though his ancestors were great men of the generation. Memories of his deeds in those days have remained for us in what is recounted in Gittin 47a, that he sold himself to the Ludim [gladiators] and relied on his strength to eradicate wickedness from the midst of the land—the sect of those who eat human flesh—and as is recounted there, he put them all to death. And this was always a common saying in his mouth, to say: "If you sold yourself to the Ludim..." as in Yerushalmi Terumot 8:3.
And likewise, even when he was already among the foremost great men of the generation, it is recounted of him in Yerushalmi Terumot, at the end of chapter 8, that robbers seized R' Imi, until R' Yonatan despaired of [saving] him; however, R' Shimon ben Lakish said: "I will pursue them, and I will kill them or I will be killed," and the end was that he rescued him from their hands.
And likewise it is recounted there that once bandits robbed R' Yoḥanan of all his money, and Resh Lakish pursued them, overtook them, and restored all his property.
And R' Yoḥanan, who knew Resh Lakish well from his youth, and saw him how little by little he turned aside from the straight path and associated with wicked men, yearned greatly to bring him back to the good. Resh Lakish was then already in the very prime of his youth, and behold, God brought [an opportunity] into his hand,

"He wanted to return to retrieve his clothes, and was unable to leap; he [R' Yoḥanan] taught him Scripture and taught him Mishnah, and made him a great man." And his toil in Torah grew so much that he turned nights into days, just as he said: "The moon was created only for study" [Eruvin 65a]. And in Yerushalmi Berakhot 1:1 they said that Resh Lakish would be so immersed in thoughts of words of Torah that he walked outside the [Sabbath] boundary on Shabbat. And he would review his Mishnah forty times corresponding to the forty days in which the Torah was given, and then enter before R' Yoḥanan, as in Ta'anit 8a. And at that time all the great men of the generation, the teachers of R' Yoḥanan, such as R' Ḥanina and R' Yannai, were still alive; and Bar Kappara, R' Yehoshua ben Levi, and R' Aphes were the great sages of the South; and R' Yehuda Nesi'ah, the grandson of R' Yehuda HaNasi, was the Nasi and head of all the sages of Israel in the Sanhedrin of Sepphoris. Therefore, when he knew within himself that he had already acquired the wisdom of the Torah, he left his home and his inheritance and went to the sages of the South to receive [traditions] from the mouth of the elders, the disciples of R' Yehuda HaNasi (and we have already explained in the entry on R' Aphes that he lived many years after R' Yehuda HaNasi and his permanent place was in the South, and only at appointed times would he come to the academy of Sepphoris, under Rabban Gamliel and R' Yehuda Nesi'ah).

And at that time he received also from R' Oshaiah; he inquired of him in Yevamot 57a; he said in his name [in] Kiddushin 80a, Pesaḥim 34b, Bekhorot 13a, Me'ilah 7b, Niddah 18b, 25a. And R' Oshaiah was so great in his eyes that he called him "the father of the Mishnah" in Yerushalmi Bava Kamma 4:6, though Resh Lakish was at that time already the great man of the generation, as is explicit in Yevamot 57a. And similarly he received from R' Ḥanina: he inquired of him in Shabbat 114a, Avodah Zarah 11b; he said in his name in Eruvin 80a; and in Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 1:2 "R' Ḥanina opened [the discourse] and R' Yoḥanan and Resh Lakish concluded." And similarly he received from R' Yannai and said in his name in Eruvin 11b, Sukkah 17b, Yoma 37b, Bava Kamma 52a, Bava Metzia 26b, Me'ilah 18a. And similarly he had discourse with R' Yonatan in Yerushalmi Eruvin 6:4. However, what we find in Ketubot 49a, "Resh Lakish in the name of R' Yosi bar Ḥanina," is a scribal error, and one must read "in the name of R' Yehuda bar Ḥanina," for so it is in Yerushalmi Ketubot 4:8. And similarly in Yerushalmi Sukkah 1:1 [and] 3, "Resh Lakish in the name of R' Yosi bar Ḥanina," one must read "R' Yehuda bar Ḥanina," as in Yerushalmi Kilayim 4:2. And similarly he had in his hand traditions from the early sages, for he said in the name of R' Elazar ben Azaryah in Bereishit Rabbah 9:3; in the name of R' Shimon ben Menasya in Vayikra Rabbah 20:2. And in Seder HaDorot he brings that Resh Lakish explains the words of Rav Avdimi bar Hamduri, and his intention is to Sukkah 20a; and begging his honor's pardon, he certainly did not have the Gemara of Sukkah before him then, for there Resh Lakish disagrees with Rav Avdimi bar Hamduri, as they said: "What is ḥutzalot? Rav Avdimi bar Hamduri said: marzuvlei. What is marzuvlei? R' Abba said: mezublei. Resh Lakish said: actual mats," and he is explaining the word "ḥutzalot."

‫וכשנפטרו כל זקני הדור ור׳ יוחנן יסד ישיבתו הגדולה בטבריא וכתר הנשיאות נתפרדה מכתר התורה כי ר' יהודה גשיאה השני לא הגיע למעלת אבותיו להיות גם ריש מתיבתא, היה רשב״ל הראש והראשון בישיבתו, ואף שבראשונה היה תלמיד ר׳ יוחגן כגיטין יט. שאמר לו ר״ל לר״י והלא למרתנו רבינו, וכן חולין קלט. וברכות לא. שאמרו בפירוש שר״י היה רבו ובמעילה ז: אר״י על ר״ל קצצתינון לרגלוהי דינוקא (לפי שר״ל היה צעיר ממנו, רש״י), אבל אח״כ נתעלה ר״ל כ״כ עד שהחשיבו ר׳ יוחנן לחבר ממש ככתובות נד: שאר״י מה אעשה שכנגדי‬ (אנוש כערכי, רש׳׳י) חולק עלי, וביבמות צב: א״ל ר״ל לר״י אי לאו דקלסך גברא רבה הוה אמינא לך וכו'.

And when all the elders of the generation passed away and R' Yoḥanan founded his great academy in Tiberias, and the crown of the Patriarchate was separated from the crown of the Torah because R' Yehuda Nesi'ah II did not reach the stature of his ancestors to be also the head of the academy, Resh Lakish was the head and the foremost in his academy. And although at first he was a disciple of R' Yoḥanan, as in Gittin 19a where Resh Lakish said to R' Yoḥanan: "Did you not teach us, our Master?" and similarly in Ḥullin 139a and Berakhot 31a where they said explicitly that R' Yoḥanan was his teacher, and in Me'ilah 7b R' Yoḥanan said concerning Resh Lakish: "You have cut off the legs of the child" (because Resh Lakish was younger than he, Rashi), nevertheless afterward Resh Lakish rose so much that R' Yoḥanan considered him an actual colleague, as in Ketubot 54b where R' Yoḥanan said: "What shall I do, for my counterpart" (a man of my own standing, Rashi) "disagrees with me?" And in Yevamot 92b Resh Lakish said to R' Yoḥanan: "Were it not that a great man praised you, I would have said to you, etc."
ור׳ יוחנן קראו מר ביומא ג:. ובעירובין פ״א ה״א כף רשב״ל לר״י וטלטל.
And R' Yoḥanan called him "Master" in Yoma 3b; and in Yerushalmi Eruvin 1:1 Resh Lakish compelled R' Yoḥanan and he carried.

וברכות פ״ח ה״ז קראו לר״י ורשב״ל שני גדולי עולם, ולא על חנם אר״י שאם אין רשב״ל בבהמ״ד חסר לו ידו אחת כירושלמי הוריות רפ״ג וסנהדרין רפ״ב, כי היה באמת כמו יר ימינו כאשר יסופר ב״ק קיז. כשבא רב כהנא מבבל לא״י וכשבא לבהמ״ד דר״י אשכחיה לר״ל דיתיב וקא מסיים מתיבתא דיומא לרבנן (ופירש״י היה‬ ‫מחזר להם מה שדרש ר״י לפי שר׳׳ל חכם גדול‬ היה ולאחר ששמעו כולם מפי הרב חוזר ומכוונה ‫בידם) אמר להו ריש לקיש היכא וכו', וזה אות ששמו היה הולך וגדול גם בבבל שר״כ שאל אך ר״ל היכא.

And in Yerushalmi Berakhot 8:7 they called R' Yoḥanan and Resh Lakish "two great men of the world." And not for naught did R' Yoḥanan say that if Resh Lakish is not in the study hall he lacks one of his hands, as in Yerushalmi Horayot start of chapter 3 and Yerushalmi Sanhedrin start of chapter 2, for he was in truth like his right hand, as is recounted in Bava Kamma 117a: when Rav Kahana came from Babylonia to Eretz Yisrael, and when he came to the study hall of R' Yoḥanan, "he found Resh Lakish sitting and concluding the daily session for the rabbis" (and Rashi explained: he was reviewing for them what R' Yoḥanan had expounded, because Resh Lakish was a great sage, and after they all heard from the mouth of the Master he would review and establish its meaning in their hands), "he said to them: 'Where is Resh Lakish?' etc." And this is a sign that his name was growing ever greater in Babylonia as well, that Rav Kahana asked only: "Where is Resh Lakish?"
ובל״ס אירע כמה פעמים כשלא היה יכול ר״י לבא למתיבתא היה אז ר״ל ‫במקים הריש מתיבתא, ולכן מצינו שהיה ‫לו מתורגמן בשם ר׳ יהודה בר נחמני‬ ‫בחגיגה טז. כתובות ח.

And without doubt it happened several times that when R' Yoḥanan was unable to come to the academy, Resh Lakish was then in the place of the head of the academy; and therefore we find that he had an interpreter [amora] named R' Yehuda bar Naḥmani in Ḥagigah 16a [and] Ketubot 8a.
ובסנהדרין כד. אמרו כל הרואה את‬ רשב״ל בבהמ״ד כאלו עוקר הרים וטוחנן‬ ‫זו בזו.
And in Sanhedrin 24a they said: "Anyone who sees Resh Lakish in the study hall, it is as though he uproots mountains and grinds them against one another."
ובכל הש״ס בבלי וירושלמי ומדרשים מלאים מהלכות ואגדות דר״י ור״ל.
And the entire Talmud, Bavli and Yerushalmi, and the midrashim are full of the halakhot and aggadot of R' Yoḥanan and Resh Lakish.

וידעו כל העם שהוא איש מורם מעם‬ ‫ויען שטבעו היה מנעוריו להשתרר ולהיות‬ ‫ראש‪ ,‬לכן ג״כ אח״כ לא נשא פני כל‬ ‫ואך האמת היה נגד עיניו, וגם להנשיא‬ ‫ר׳ יהודה נשיאה השני לא נשא פניו כאשר יסופר בירושלמי הוריות רפ״ג‬ וסנהדרין רפ״ב שאר״ל נשיא שחטא מלקין אותו בב״ד של ג׳ — שמע ר״י נשייא וכעס, וברח ר״ל לדא מוגדלא או‬ ‫לכפר חיטיא, למחר סלק ר׳ יוחנן לבית ועדא וסלק ר״י נשיא לבית ועדא ושאל לר״י למה לית מרי א״ל מילה דאורייתא שרי טפח בחדא ידיה א״ל ובחרא טפחין?‬ ‫א״ל יען שחסר לי ירי האחרת והוא ר״ל‪,‬‬ ‫אמר לו למחר אגא ואת גיפיק לקרמיה‪,‬‬ ‫וכשבאו להוציאו אייל ר״ל להגשיא מה‬ ‫אתון םברין מה דחיל מיגכון הויגא מגע‬ ‫אולפנא דרחמנא ? ואז אירע שדבי גשיאה‬ ‫אוקמו דיינא דלא הוה גמיר‪ ,‬מה עשה‬ ר״ל אוקמיה ליהודה בר נחמני מתורגמניה

And all the people knew that he was a man exalted above the people. And because his nature from his youth was to rule and to be a leader, therefore also afterward he did not show favoritism to anyone, and only the truth was before his eyes. And even to the Nasi, R' Yehuda Nesi'ah the Second, he did not show favoritism, as is recounted in Yerushalmi Horayot at the start of chapter 3 and Yerushalmi Sanhedrin at the start of chapter 2, where Resh Lakish said: "A Nasi who sinned, they flog him in a court of three." R' Yehuda Nesi'ah heard and became angry, and Resh Lakish fled to the enclosure of Magdala or to Kefar Ḥittaya. On the next day, R' Yoḥanan went up to the study hall, and R' Yehuda Nesi'ah went up to the study hall and asked R' Yoḥanan: "Why is my master not [teaching]?" He said to him: "Wait to say a word of Torah." He clapped with one of his hands, and said to him: "Do they clap with one [hand]?" He said to him: "Because my other hand is missing, and that is Resh Lakish." He said to him: "Tomorrow I and you will go out to meet him." And when they came to bring him out, Resh Lakish said to the Nasi: "What do you think, that because I fear you I would withhold the teaching of the Merciful One?!" And at that time it happened that the household of the Nasi appointed a judge who was not learned. What did Resh Lakish do? He appointed Yehuda bar Naḥmani as his interpreter [meturgeman],
‫וקם גחין עליה ולא אמר לו ולא מידי, פתח ואמר הוי אומר לעץ וכו׳ כסנהדדין ז:.
and he stood and bent over him, and he did not say anything to him. He opened and said: "'Woe to him who says to wood, [Awake]!' etc.," as in Sanhedrin 7b.
אבל אח״כ נעשו אוהבים ז״לז כע״ז ו: ‬ששאל ר״י נשיאה לר״ל מה יעשה עם הדינרא ששדר לו ההוא מינא ביום אידו ור״ל אסר לו כירושלמי ע״ז רפ״א שר״ל ביקש לגדור הדבר.

However, afterward they became friends with one another, as in Avodah Zarah 6b, where R' Yehuda Nesi'ah asked Resh Lakish what he should do with the dinar that a certain heretic sent him on his festival day, and Resh Lakish forbade it to him; and as in Yerushalmi Avodah Zarah at the start of chapter 1, that Resh Lakish sought to make a fence around the matter.
וכן ב״ב ז‪ .‬כשהנשיא רמא שורא אדרבנן א״ל ר״ל רבנן לא צריכי נטירותא.
And similarly in Bava Batra 7a, when the Nasi imposed the [tax for the] wall upon the Rabbis, Resh Lakish said to him: "The Rabbis do not need protection."
ובשבת קיט‪ .‬אמר לו כך מקובלני —‬ מאבותיך כל עיר שאין בה תינוקית של בית רבן מחריבין אותה ועי״ז שלח הנשיא לר׳ חייא ב״א ור׳ אסי ור׳ אמי לעבור בכל ערי ישראל כחגיגה פ״א ה״ז.

And in Shabbat 119b, he said to him: "Thus have I received a tradition from your ancestors: Every city in which there are no school-children, they destroy it." And through this the Nasi sent R' Ḥiyya bar Abba and R' Assi and R' Ammi to pass through all the cities of Eretz Yisrael, as in Yerushalmi Ḥagigah 1:7.
והנשיא היה מיכן תמיד לעזור לר״ל בכח הנשיאות שלו, כאשר יסופר כתובות פ״ט ה״ב שאייתי רשב״ל עבדוי דר״י נשיא ואפיק מינה.

And the Nasi was always ready to help Resh Lakish with the power of his patriarchate, as is recounted in Yerushalmi Ketubot 9:2, that Resh Lakish brought the servants of R' Yehuda Nesi'ah and exacted [payment] from her.
ובברכות מד. יסיפר שפ״א אכל ר״ל פ־רות גינוסר עד דמריד ושדר ר״י נשיאה באלושי אבתריה והביאהו לביתו.
And in Berakhot 44a it is recounted that once Resh Lakish ate the fruits of Ginosar until he became delirious, and R' Yehuda Nesi'ah sent searchers after him and brought him to his house.

And in Bereshit Rabbah 78:12: Resh Lakish went up to inquire after the welfare of Rabbenu (and that is R' Yehuda Nesi'ah the Second, for all the Nesi'im were called by the name Rabbi or Rabbenu). He said to him: "Pray for me, for this kingdom is very wicked." He said to him: "Do not take anything from any person, and you will not have to give anything."

I cite an entire Mishnah, and you say, etc." This was not, Heaven forbid, out of malice of heart, or because he had some personal hatred against R' Elazar; rather, because R' Elazar was like a disciple-colleague to Resh Lakish, as we find in Bekhorot 26b: "R' Elazar said in the name of Resh Lakish." And similarly in Menaḥot 93b, where R' Elazar went and stated a teaching of Resh Lakish and did not state it in his name, Resh Lakish took offense; and Resh Lakish raised difficulties against his own words, and R' Elazar was silent. And after Resh Lakish's mind was appeased, he said to him: "Why did you not say to me, etc." And therefore, it was not for nothing that Resh Lakish took offense at him, and this was in order to set him on the path of truth, to say a thing in the name of the one who said it—concerning which R' Yoḥanan himself was also very strict. And similarly, the incident of Sanhedrin 26a, regarding his calling R' Ḥiyya bar Zarnuki and R' Shimon ben Yehotzadak "cattle herders"—justice was with him, because they provoked Resh Lakish, as is explained there, and R' Yoḥanan also justified Resh Lakish. And where truth was concerned, he did not show favoritism even to R' Yoḥanan, as in Sanhedrin 96a, where he said: "Better is that of the blacksmith (R' Yitzḥak Nappaḥa) than that of the son of the blacksmith (R' Yoḥanan)." Among his precious traits, we find in Berakhot 31a that he did not fill his mouth with laughter from the day he heard from R' Yoḥanan that it is forbidden to do so. And he acknowledged the truth, as in Yerushalmi Demai 2:3, that Resh Lakish went up to those of the house of R' Yannai, and the women fled from him so that they would not touch him; he said to them: "I am an am ha-aretz regarding purities." And among his precious sayings, in Berakhot 5a: "A person should always incite the good inclination against the evil inclination"; "Whoever engages in Torah, sufferings are kept away from him." And there on 8a: "Whoever has a synagogue in his city and does not enter there to pray is called a bad neighbor." And there on 10b: "What is 'kir'? From the walls [kirot] of his heart." And in Eruvin 99a he said: "One who expectorates before his master is liable to death." And in Yerushalmi Berakhot at the end of chapter 9, he warned his disciples and said that they should be diligent in the Torah constantly, for "If you forsake me for one day, I will forsake you for two days."

With all his greatness and glory, he did not derive benefit from the honor of the Torah, but supported himself from his own property, and he himself guarded his orchards, as in Moed Katan 17a: "Resh Lakish was guarding an orchard. A certain man came and was eating figs. He shouted at him, and he paid no attention to him, so he excommunicated him. That man said to him: 'On the contrary, let that man (Resh Lakish) be under excommunication! Even if I have become liable to you for money, have I become liable to you for excommunication?' He came to the study hall, and they said to him: 'His is a valid excommunication; yours is not a valid excommunication,'" and he had to go to the house of the Patriarch so that they would annul it for him.
And in Dor Dor ve-Dorshav, Part 3, page 72, he says: "After all the greatness of Resh Lakish, he did not merit to sit as head. However, there is no wonder in this — for in one matter Resh Lakish opposed the majority of the sages of his generation, and that was regarding the examination of the external mishnayot [beraitot] — and he established a rule and publicized it: 'Any teaching that was not taught in the academy, we do not rely upon it' (Yerushalmi Eruvin 1:6). And not only did he act according to this rule with the average sages of the generation, but even to R' Yoḥanan he did not show favor, and he refused to accept a beraita from him, saying: 'We have no need of this, for R' Yehuda HaNasi taught us a complete mishnah' (Yerushalmi Kilayim 1:6; Yerushalmi Bava Kamma, end of chapter 5) — and now the matter will be understood why Resh Lakish, with all his wisdom and virtues, did not succeed in rising to sit as head, and sat until the day of his death before R' Yoḥanan." Thus far his words.
Now, as for the eulogy he makes over Resh Lakish and his bad fortune, his heart aches in vain. For without doubt, had Resh Lakish wanted to separate from his brother-in-law and beloved teacher, he would then have gone to another city and established a great yeshiva there, since the Sanhedrin had already been abolished from Israel and only houses of Torah took their place. And inasmuch as we see that Resh Lakish sat all his days with R' Yoḥanan, it is a sign of the preciousness of his heart, that his entire aim and desire was that the center of Torah should be in one place. And as is known, R' Yoḥanan was not only the head of the generation in Eretz Yisrael, but also in Babylonia his words were heeded like the words of the Urim after the passing of Rav and Shmuel. And Resh Lakish merited this good name just like R' Yoḥanan, for the halakhot of both of them were brought equally to the yeshivot of Babylonia. And had he lived after R' Yoḥanan, then without doubt Resh Lakish would have been the head of the yeshiva after him. However, because in his youth R' Yoḥanan was the primary teacher of Resh Lakish and was also older than him, therefore R' Yoḥanan reigned, and Resh Lakish could not reach the level of R' Yoḥanan, for "there is one leader for a generation." However, we have already explained above that Resh Lakish was like the right hand of R' Yoḥanan, and sometimes also stood in place of the head of the yeshiva; therefore we need not be distressed over this, for Resh Lakish too was never distressed in his days.
However, regarding what the scholar Weiss wrote, that he also did not show favor to R' Yoḥanan and this was his sin for which he did not succeed in rising and sitting as head — begging his honor's pardon, he erred in the simple meaning of the text in Yerushalmi Kilayim and Bava Kamma there (which is a single passage). And this is the wording of the Yerushalmi there: "The wolf and the dog... although they resemble one another, they are kilayim [forbidden mixtures] with one another." And the Gemara there asks: "Have we not taught [this regarding] a bird? R' Yoḥanan said: 'I brought it from that of Bar Dalia,' (who said): 'The rooster with the pheasant and with the peacock, although they resemble one another, they are kilayim with one another.'" And regarding this Resh Lakish came and said: "R' Yehuda HaNasi taught a complete mishnah: 'And similarly beasts and birds that are like them.'" And so it is literally in Bava Kamma 55a, and there only the words of Resh Lakish are brought on the Mishnah, who said: "Here R' Yehuda HaNasi taught that the rooster, peacock, and pheasant are kilayim with one another." And it is a simple matter to any student that at first glance R' Yoḥanan did not notice that R' Yehuda HaNasi had already stated it anonymously in the Mishnah, and therefore he wanted to prove the law from the beraita of Bar Dalia, and Resh Lakish stood him upon the truth that we do not need this because the law was already taught in the Mishnah. And this is literally like what Ilfa said in Taanit 21a, that for all the beraitot of R' Ḥiyya and R' Oshaia he could show their source in the Mishnah of R' Yehuda HaNasi. And R' Yoḥanan said literally thus to R' Yannai his teacher in Makkot 21b: when R' Yannai said, "One who covers himself with kilayim is lashed," R' Yoḥanan said to him, "Is this not our Mishnah?" And similarly we find this expression throughout the Talmud; and if so, what refusal is there in the matter? Behold, he only stood him upon the truth.
And as for what the aforementioned scholar said, that he established the rule and publicized it: "Any teaching that was not taught in the academy, we do not rely upon it" — this scholar has made us laugh! Behold, a rule greater than this is already known and famous, namely what they said in Ḥullin 141a, that any beraita that was not taught in the school of R' Ḥiyya and R' Oshaia is corrupted. And sound common sense dictates that if some student came to the study hall and brought a beraita in his hand, they did not accept it from him until they investigated and inquired whether one may rely upon him and whether it is not corrupted in his hand.
Furthermore, he did not see what is explicit in Yerushalmi Gittin 3:1: "R' Yosi bar R' Bun said: It is not that Resh Lakish was contentious against R' Yoḥanan; rather... when he heard a beraita he relied upon it, and when he did not hear a beraita he nullified his own opinion before the opinion of R' Yoḥanan."
His students and those who reported his statements: Almost all the students of R' Yoḥanan were also students of Resh Lakish, such as: R' Abba said in the name of Resh Lakish, as in Shabbat 63a; Gittin 3b. R' Abba bar Zavda in his name, as in Yerushalmi Sheviit 2:5. R' Abba bar Kahana in his name, as in Yerushalmi Kilayim 3, end of halakhah 1. R' Avduma of Ḥaifa in his name, as in Yerushalmi Terumot 3:3. R' Abbahu said in the name of Resh Lakish, as in Berakhot 47a; Pesaḥim 46a; Beitzah 13a; Pesikta de-Rav Kahana 131b. R' Avin bar Ḥiyya said before Resh Lakish, as in Yerushalmi Terumot 6, end of halakhah 1. R' Aivo in his name, in Pesaḥim 46a. R' Ila'a said in the name of Resh Lakish, as in Ketubot 49b. R' Shalmoni in his name in Bereishit Rabbah 68:12. R' Shimon bar Abba (so one must read, and there [it is written] R' Yishmael) said to Resh Lakish: "Thus said R' Yehoshua ben Levi." He said to him: "Sit opposite me" (May your strength be firm [well done!]) in Ḥullin 122a. R' Shimon ben Elyakim raised a difficulty to Resh Lakish in Avodah Zarah 34b. Shimon bar Narshiya in his name in Yerushalmi Kilayim 3, at the end of halakhah 1 and the end of halakhah 4.
His wives, his sons, his household, his passing, and the length of his days.
All the biographers of our Rabbis did not notice that Resh Lakish had two wives: one was the sister of R' Yoḥanan, and the second he married in his old age, and she bore him sons, and when he passed away he left behind young orphans; and we will explain this with clear proofs. Behold, we have already brought above the incident of Bava Metzia 84a, how R' Yoḥanan brought him back to the good path [repentance] and said to him: "I will give you my sister, who is more beautiful than I." And Resh Lakish was then in the very prime of his youth and his strength, and without doubt R' Yoḥanan fulfilled his promise and he married his sister. And it is known that R' Yoḥanan from the day he was born had neither father nor mother, as is explicit in Kiddushin 31b; if so, his sister was either his older sister or was born a twin with R' Yoḥanan. And it is recounted in Bava Metzia there: "One day they were disputing in the study hall regarding a sword... from when is their manufacture complete? R' Yoḥanan said: From when one tempers them in the furnace; and Resh Lakish said: From when one polishes them in water. He [R' Yoḥanan] said to him: A brigand knows his brigandage! He [Resh Lakish] said to him: And how have you benefited me? There they called me Master, here they call me Master! He said to him: I benefited you by bringing you under the wings of the Shekhinah. R' Yoḥanan felt offended; Resh Lakish fell ill. His sister came and was weeping. She said to him: Do it for the sake of my sons! He said to her: 'Leave your orphans, I will keep them alive' [Jeremiah 49:11]... Resh Lakish's soul rested, and R' Yoḥanan was grieving after him greatly." And when they brought R' Elazar ben Pedat to R' Yoḥanan, he said to him: "Are you like Bar Lakisha? Bar Lakisha, when I would state a matter, would raise twenty-four difficulties against me, etc." He would go and rend his garments and weep and say: "Where are you, Bar Lakisha?" And he was screaming until his mind left him; the Rabbis begged for mercy upon him and his soul rested. Now, although all this incident is brought in a poetic and aggadic manner — for in truth, from the day that R' Yoḥanan bathed in the Jordan until Resh Lakish passed away, several decades passed, as is known that R' Yoḥanan lived a very long life, more than a hundred years, and Resh Lakish, even though he was younger than him by approximately ten years, was then approximately about twenty-five years old, and similarly we explained that R' Yoḥanan did not pass away immediately after Resh Lakish, and lived approximately about three years after him; therefore there was between one incident and the other close to seventy years — nevertheless, such is the way of our Sages of blessed memory, to recount only the main points of the stories, their beginning and their end. And according to these true words, how can we say that Resh Lakish left behind young sons who were dependent on their father's table — "shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear?" [Genesis 17:17]. And even more explicit is Taanit 9a, that R' Yoḥanan found the young child of Resh Lakish. He said to him: "Recite to me your verse." He said to him: "'You shall surely tithe,' etc." And furthermore, R' Yoḥanan found the young child of Resh Lakish sitting and saying: "'The foolishness of a man,' etc." He raised his eyes and looked at him. His mother came and took him away. She said to him: "Come away from before him, so that he should not do to you as he did to your father." And from this we see explicitly that Resh Lakish left behind a young son. And how is such a thing possible? Rather, it is clear to us that R' Yoḥanan's sister bore him sons, as is explicit in Ketubot 8b, that R' Ḥiyya bar Abba was the Bible teacher and Mishnah teacher of the "sons" of Resh Lakish, and it is explicit there that a young child of his died during his lifetime. And likewise he had a daughter, in Gittin 47a, where it is recounted

And when his wife, the sister of R' Yoḥanan, died, he then married a wife in his old age, and she bore him sons, and therefore when Resh Lakish passed away he indeed left behind young sons. And only a small error fell into Bava Metzia 84a, and instead of "his sister [aḥateih] came" one must read "his wife [itteteih] came," and this is a small error in a manuscript between [the letters] ḥet and tav. And even though it is against the opinion of our master Rashi, who explains there that she was the sister of R' Yoḥanan, nevertheless it is known that our early masters were not precise in this, or that it is from some student who thought that the two stories there are one. And a support for this I found in Dikdukei Soferim, which brings from a manuscript: "his wife [deveit'hu] came." And they said in Gittin 47a: When Resh Lakish passed away, he left a kav of saffron, and he applied to himself [the verse]: "And leave their wealth to others" [Psalms 49:11]. And according to what we have said, Resh Lakish lived a long life of approximately more than ninety years, and R' Yoḥanan did not find his replacement until he weakened and passed away through this.

div.head: R' Shimon bar Naḥman.
div.ab: כן מביא באוצר ישראל בשמות האמוראים משהש״ר פ״א־טז, ונזדמן לו מדרש שאינו מוגה כי במדרשים שלנו איתא שם ר' שמואל בן נחמן הנודע.

So he brings in Otzar Yisrael among the names of the Amoraim from Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:16, and an unrevised midrash chanced into his hand, for in our midrashim it is stated there the well-known R' Shmuel ben Naḥman.

div.head: R' Shimon ben Menasya. (A Tanna mentioned in the Mishnah).
div.ab: הוא היה תלמיד ר״מ כדמוכח כתובות יד: ‬ר״ש בן אלעזר אומר משום ר״מ וכן היה ר״ש בן מנשיא אומר כדבריו.
He was a disciple of R' Meir, as is proven in Ketubot 14b: "R' Shimon ben Elazar says in the name of R' Meir, and so R' Shimon ben Menasya used to say in accordance with his words."
וב״מ קו: רש״בג אומר משום ר״מ וכן היה רש״במ אומר כדבריו.
And in Bava Metzia 106b: "Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel [R' Shimon ben Elazar] says in the name of R' Meir, and so R' Shimon ben Menasya used to say in accordance with his words."
ובנדה כא: סומכוס אומר משום ר״מ וכן היה רש״במ אומר כדבריו.
And in Niddah 21b: "Sumkhos says in the name of R' Meir, and so R' Shimon ben Menasya used to say in accordance with his words."
וכן קבל מרש״בי כאבות פ״ו־ט‬
And similarly he received [traditions] from R' Shimon ben Yoḥai, as in Avot 6:9.
(הנדפס במשנה) ר״ש בן מנסיא‬ אומר משום רש״בי הנוי והכח וכו'.
(which is printed in the Mishnah): "R' Shimon ben Menasya says in the name of R' Shimon bar Yoḥai: 'Beauty, strength, etc.'"
ובספרי בהעלותך פסוק ויצעק רש״במ אומר אלו הזקנים, והמאמר מובא ויק"ר פ״טו־כד ותנחומא שם ושם איתא פליגא בה ר״ש בר אבא ור״ש בן מנסיא, והוא ט״ס וצ״ל רש"בי ורש״במ כדמובא בהערה שם.

And in Sifrei Behaalotekha on the verse "And he cried out" [Numbers 11:2], "R' Shimon ben Menasya says: 'These are the elders,'" and this statement is brought in Vayikra Rabbah 15:24 [?] and Tanḥuma there, and there it is stated: "R' Shimon bar Abba and R' Shimon ben Menasya disagree about this," and this is a scribal error and one must read "R' Shimon bar Yoḥai and R' Shimon ben Menasya," as is brought in the note there.
ונזכר במשנה חגיגה פ״א מ״ז אמר איזהו מעוות שאינו יכול לתקון זח הבא על הערוה והוליד ממנה ממזר.
And he is mentioned in the Mishnah, Ḥagigah 1:7: He said, "What is 'that which is crooked and cannot be made straight'? This is one who has forbidden sexual relations and begets a mamzer from her."

והיה כחבר לרבי שחולק עמו פא׳׳פ‬ ‫כביצה כי‪ .‬ת״ר בכור הם שנפל לבור‬ ‫ר' יהודה הנשיא אומר — א״ל ריש בן‬ ‫מנםיא הרי אמרו ובו׳‪.‬‬ ‫והואור׳ יוסי בן המשולם היו נקראץ‬ ‫בשם עדה קדושה כמע״ש פ״ב ה״ר‪,‬‬ ‫ומפורש בקה״ר פ״ט פסוק ראה חיים‬ ‫אמר ר׳ משום עדה קרושה קנה לך‬ ‫אומנות עם התורה — ולמה הוא קורא‬ ‫אותן עדה קדושה ששם היו ר׳ יוסי בן‬ ‫משולם ורש״במ שתיו משלשין היום‬ ‫שליש לתורה‪ ,‬שליש ‪.‬לתפלה‪ ,‬שליש‬ ‫למלאכה‪.‬‬ ‫ובםה״ד האריך מובא אם רש״במ נקרא‬ ‫גם בשם קהלה קדישא המובא ביצה‬ ‫בז‪ ,.‬ובאמת איגם שייכין ז״לז באשר‬ ‫בארתי בערך קהלה קדישא‪.‬‬ ‫הלכותיו בברייתא מציגו שבת מב‪.‬‬ ‫שאסיר ליתן באמבטי בשבת י בין חמץ‬ ‫לתוך צינן וכוי‪.‬‬ ‫ומגילה ז‪ .‬קהלת אינו מטמא את הירים‪.‬‬ ‫ומ״ק ד‪ .‬ערוגות זו למעלה מזו לא‬ ‫ידלה מן התחתוגה‪.‬‬ ‫יבתיבית בז‪ :‬ולו תהיי לאשה אשר‪.‬‬ ‫הראייה לקיימה‪.‬‬ ‫יגיטץ מט‪ .‬שיר של הקדש שגגת שיר‬ ‫של הדיוט פטיר יכו'‪,‬‬ ‫וב״ב קלב‪ — .‬שאם בא בנו אץ מתנתו‬ ‫מתנה‪.‬‬
