And he was like a colleague to R' Yehuda HaNasi, as he disagrees with him face to face in Beitzah 26a: "Our Rabbis taught: A flawless firstborn animal that fell into a pit, R' Yehuda HaNasi says... R' Shimon ben Menasya said to him: 'Behold, they have already said, etc.'" And he and R' Yosi ben ha-Meshullam were called by the name "Edah Kedoshah" (Holy Congregation), as in Yerushalmi Maaser Sheni 2:4, and it is explained in Kohelet Rabbah, chapter 9, on the verse "Enjoy life": "R' Yehuda HaNasi said in the name of the Edah Kedoshah: 'Acquire a craft for yourself along with the Torah'—and why does he call them Edah Kedoshah? Because R' Yosi ben Meshullam and R' Shimon ben Menasya were there, who used to divide the day into thirds: a third for Torah, a third for prayer, and a third for work." And in Seder ha-Dorot he discussed at length [bringing sources on] whether R' Shimon ben Menasya was also called by the name "Kehillah Kaddisha" (Holy Community), which is brought in Beitzah 27a; and in truth they have no connection to one another, as I have explained in the entry "Kehillah Kaddisha." His halakhot in the Baraita we find in Shabbat 42a: that it is forbidden to pour into a bath on Shabbat, whether hot water into cold water, etc. And Megillah 7a: "Kohelet does not render the hands impure." And Moed Katan 4a: "Garden beds one above the other, he may not draw water from the lower one." And Ketubot 37b: "'And she shall be to him for a wife'—a woman who is fit for him to keep." And Gittin 49a: "An ox of the Temple treasury—an unwitting offense regarding an ox of a commoner is exempt, etc." And Bava Batra 132a: "...that if his son comes back, his gift is not a valid gift."
‫ובע״ז נג‪ .‬ע״ז של ישראל אץ לה‬ ‫בטילה עולמית.

The Hebrew of this paragraph on Wikisource is uncorrected OCR (columns mixed, letters confused). The translation is not reliable; read the scan. And in Avodah Zarah 53a: "An idol belonging to an Israelite can never be nullified."

‫וזבחים צד‪ .‬עוצבא שחשב עליה לקצעה‬ ‫טהורה ער שיקציענה‪.‬‬ ‫ושם צג‪ :‬שאםור לשבור עצם בקרבן‬ ‫פםח אפילו עצם שאץ בו מוח‪.‬‬ ‫ובתוספתא תרומות פ״ח אומר אין לך‬ ‫גרב ובו‪/‬‬ ‫ומה שטציגו ב״ק גט‪ .‬ר' שמעון בן‬ ‫יהודה אומר משום ר״ש בן מגםיא אוגס‬ ‫איגו משלם את הצער הוא ט״ס וצ״ל‬ ‫משום ר׳ שמעון בן יוחאי‪ ,‬וכן הוא‬ ‫בבתובית לט‪ .‬ובן הוא בדק״ס ב״ק שם‬ ‫בכל הב״י והיה יכתוב רש״בי וגעשה מן‬ ‫היו״ד מ״ם‪ ,‬ולא צדק בזה דוה״ר בח״ב‬ ‫צד ‪ .58‬וכן הוא מפורש בירושלמי כתובות‬ ‫פ״ג רה׳׳ה ר׳ שמעון פטר את האוגם מן‬ ‫הצער‪.‬‬ ‫דבריו באגרה מציגו ברכות סא‪ .‬אמר‬ ‫מלמד שקלעה הקב״ה לחוה ובו‪ /‬ובגדה‬ ‫מ ה ‪ :‬מובא המאמר שר״ל אמר בשמו‪.‬‬ ‫וביומא פה‪ :‬דרש הפסוק ושמרו ב״י‬ ‫את השבת אמרה תורה חלל עליו שבת‬ ‫אחת כרי שישמור שבתות הרבה‪,‬‬ ‫ובמגילה טו‪ :‬מה ראתה אסתר שזימגח‬ ‫את המן אולי ירגיש המקום ויעשה גס‪.‬‬ ‫ובםגהדרין גט‪ .‬אמר חבל על שמש‬ ‫גדול שאבד מן העולם‪.‬‬ ‫וב״ר רפ״םג אמר מנין שאפילו הקב״ה‬ ‫מתמלא רחמים עליו בשעה שהוא יגע‬ ‫בחורה וכוי‪.‬‬ ‫ובויק״ר פ״כ־־ב רש״בל בשמו שתפוח‬ ‫עקיבו של אדם היה מכהה גלגל חמה‪,‬‬ ‫וצ״ל ר' לוי בשמו כדמובא המאמר‬ ‫תגחומא אחרייג וחוקת־יז‪.‬‬ ‫ורבי וב״ב היו גדולים מאוד בעיגיו‬ ‫כאבות פ״ו־ט אר״ש בן מגסיא אלו שבע‬ ‫מדות שמגו חכמים לצדיקים כולןגתקיימו‬ ‫ברבי ובגיו‪ ,‬והמאמר הזה מובא באריכות‬ ‫בירושלמי סנהדרין פ״יא ה״ג ר״ש בן

The Hebrew of this paragraph on Wikisource is uncorrected OCR (columns mixed, letters confused). The translation is not reliable; read the scan. And Zevaḥim 94a: "A saddle-cloth that he intended to scrape is pure until he scrapes it." And there 97b: that it is forbidden to break a bone in the Pesach offering, even a bone that has no marrow in it. And in Tosefta Terumot chapter 8 he says: "You have no barrel, etc." And that which we find in Bava Kamma 39a: "R' Shimon ben Yehudah says in the name of R' Shimon ben Menasya: 'A rapist does not pay for pain,'" is a scribal error, and one must read "in the name of R' Shimon ben Yoḥai," and so it is in Ketubot 39a, and so it is in Dikdukei Soferim to Bava Kamma there in all the manuscripts, and it was written רש"בי [R' Shimon bar Yoḥai] and the yod was turned into a mem; and Dorot ha-Rishonim in part 2, page 58, was not correct in this. And so it is explicit in Yerushalmi Ketubot 3:5 (beginning of the halakhah): "R' Shimon exempted the rapist from [paying for] pain." His words in Aggadah we find in Berakhot 61a: He said, "This teaches that the Holy One, blessed be He, braided Eve's hair, etc.," and in Niddah 45b this statement is brought that Resh Lakish said in his name. And in Yoma 85b he expounded the verse "And the children of Israel shall keep the Shabbat": "The Torah said, 'Profane one Shabbat on his account so that he may keep many Shabbatot.'" And in Megillah 15b: "What did Esther see that she invited Haman? 'Perhaps the Omnipresent will notice and perform a miracle.'" And in Sanhedrin 59b he said: "Alas for a great servant that has been lost to the world." And Bereishit Rabbah, beginning of chapter 63, he said: "From where [do we know] that even the Holy One, blessed be He, is filled with mercy for him at the time that he toils in Torah, etc." And in Vayikra Rabbah 20:2, Resh Lakish in his name: that the ball of Adam's heel dimmed the globe of the sun; and one must read "R' Levi in his name," as the statement is brought in Tanḥuma Aḥarei 3 and Ḥukkat 17. And R' Yehuda HaNasi and his household were very great in his eyes, as in Avot 6:8: R' Shimon ben Menasya said, "These seven qualities that the Sages enumerated for the righteous were all fulfilled in R' Yehuda HaNasi and his sons," and this statement is brought at length in Yerushalmi Sanhedrin 11:3: "R' Shimon ben

מנסיא אומר הנוי והכח וכו' לצדיקים נאה להם ונאה לעולם, תני ר״ש בן גמליאל [צ״ל בן מנסיא] אומר אלו שבע מדות שמנו חכמים בצדיקים היו ברבי, מאן רבי הוא ר' יהודה הנשיא, א״ר אבהו הוא רבי הוא ר׳ יודן הנשיא הוא רבינו.

Menasya says: 'Beauty, strength, etc. for the righteous is becoming to them and becoming to the world.' It was taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel [one must read: R' Shimon ben Menasya] says: 'These seven qualities that the Sages enumerated in the righteous were in R' Yehuda HaNasi.' Who is R' Yehuda HaNasi? He is R' Yehuda HaNasi. R' Abbahu said: 'He is R' Yehuda HaNasi, he is R' Yudan HaNasi, he is Rabbenu.'"

וכבר תמה ע״ז בדוה״ר ח״ב צד ‪56‬ ורצה לשבש שם, אבל נראה בפשטות, כי ידוע שרש״במ היה חבר רבי ואפשר שהיה זקן ממנו, והוא ראה אך את רבי שהוא הגיע לזקנה ושיבה, אבל את בניו לא ראה אם האריכו ימים כאביהם כי באמת בנו ר״ג לא האריך ימים וגם כבודו לא היה גדול ככבוד רבינו הקדוש ‫שלא היה ממלא מקומו בתורה, ולכן ארש״במ הלשון בדרך כלל אלו שבע מדות כולן נתקיימו ברבי ובניו, פי׳ לכולם ביחד היו השבע מדות, אבל ר׳ יוחנן שראה בעיניו את רבינו הקדוש ואת בנו ר״ג שלא בא לכלל אבותיו לא בשנים ולא בחכמה, ובימיו היה ר׳ יהודה נשיאה ג״כ גדול הדור, לכן אמר כל שבע מדות היו (אך) ברבי, וכדי שלא נטעה שכונתו על שאר הנשיאים שכולם נקראין בשם רבי לכן מפרש מאן רבי הוא ר׳ יהודה הנשיא, ואף שר״י נשיאה היה ג״כ גדול הדור אבל אפשר כשאמר זאת לא היה עדיין ר' יהודה נשיאה הגיע לשנות שיבה, אבל ר' אבהו שהיה תלמידו דר״י וזכה עוד להכיר את ר״י נשיאה וגדולתו ותפארתו לכן בא והוסיף הוא רבי הוא ר׳ יודן הנשיא הוא רבינו, שגם בו נתקיימו כל הז׳ מדות.

And in Dorot ha-Rishonim, part 2, page 56, he already wondered about this and wanted to emend it as a corruption there. However, it seems simple, for it is known that R' Shimon ben Menasya was a colleague of R' Yehuda HaNasi and it is possible that he was older than him, and he only saw R' Yehuda HaNasi reach old age and hoary head, whereas regarding his sons, he did not see whether they lived long like their father; for in truth, his son Rabban Gamliel did not live long, and also his honor was not as great as the honor of R' Yehuda HaNasi, as he did not fill his place in Torah. Therefore, R' Shimon ben Menasya stated the phrasing in a general way: "These seven qualities were all fulfilled in R' Yehuda HaNasi and his sons," meaning: all of them together possessed the seven qualities. However, R' Yoḥanan, who saw with his own eyes R' Yehuda HaNasi and his son Rabban Gamliel—who did not reach the level of his fathers, neither in years nor in wisdom—and in his days R' Yehuda Nesiah was also the great man of the generation, therefore he said, "All seven qualities were (only) in R' Yehuda HaNasi"; and so that we should not err that his intention was regarding the other Patriarchs, all of whom are called by the name "Rabbi," he therefore explains: "Who is Rabbi? He is R' Yehuda HaNasi." And even though R' Yehuda Nesiah was also the great man of the generation, it is possible that when he said this, R' Yehuda Nesiah had not yet reached the years of hoary age. However, R' Abbahu, who was the disciple of R' Yoḥanan and merited further to know R' Yehuda Nesiah and his greatness and his glory, therefore came and added: "He is Rabbi, he is R' Yudan HaNasi, he is Rabbenu"—that in him too all the seven qualities were fulfilled.

div.head: R' Shimon bar Nezira.
div.ab: נזכר שבת לג: על המאמר שאמר ר׳ גוריון ואיתימא רב יוסף בר שמעיה בזמן שהצדיקים בדור — א״ר יצחק בר זעירא ואמרי לה ר' שמעון בן נזירא מאי קראה וכו׳‬

He is mentioned in Shabbat 33b on the statement that R' Gurion — and some say Rav Yosef bar Shemayah — said: "At a time when the righteous are in the generation" — R' Yitzḥak bar Zeira — and some say it was R' Shimon ben Nezira — said: "What is its verse?" etc.

וביבמות צז. א״ר יוחנן משום רש״בי כל ת״ח שאומרים שמועה מפיו בע״הז שפתותיו וכו׳ א״ר יצחק בן זעירא ואיתימא שמעון נזירא מאי קראה וכו', והמאמר הזה מובא שקלים ספ״ב שמעון בן נזירא בשם ר׳ יצחק אמר כל ת״ח וכו׳.

And in Yevamot 97a: R' Yoḥanan said in the name of R' Shimon bar Yoḥai: "Every Torah scholar in whose name a tradition is recited in this world, his lips [move in the grave]," etc.; R' Yitzḥak ben Zeira — and some say Shimon Nezira — said: "What is its verse?" etc. And this statement is brought in Yerushalmi Shekalim at the end of chapter 2: Shimon ben Nezira in the name of R' Yitzḥak said: "Every Torah scholar," etc.
‫ובירושלמי מו״ק פ״ג סה״ז בר טירא אמר האומר שמועה משם אומרה שפתותיו רוחשות בקבר וכו׳ ובל״ס צ״ל בר נזירא ומנו״ן וזי״ן נעשה טי״ת.

And in Yerushalmi Moed Katan chapter 3, end of halakhah 7: Bar Tira said: "One who recites a tradition in the name of the one who said it, his lips whisper in the grave," etc. And without doubt one must read "Bar Nezira", and from the nun and zayin a tet was formed.
ומזה אנו רואין שבר נזירא הוא ר״ש בר נזירא, ובשם זה מצינו אותו שקלים ספ״ב בר נזירא אומר כהדין דשתי קונדיטון, ר׳ יצחק אומר כהדין וכו'.

And from this we see that Bar Nezira is R' Shimon bar Nezira, and by this name we find him in Yerushalmi Shekalim at the end of chapter 2: Bar Nezira says: "Like this one who drinks spiced wine [konditon]"; R' Yitzḥak says: "Like this one," etc.
וכן נזכר בשם זה בשהש״ר פ״א־יד.
And likewise he is mentioned by this name in Shir HaShirim Rabbah 1:14.
ונזכר בהלכה בשבת פ״ב ה״ג ר' אחא ר׳ סימון בשם ר׳ שמעון נזירא עשאה מזור טהורה וכו'.
And he is mentioned in halakhah in Yerushalmi Shabbat 2:3: R' Aḥa, R' Simon in the name of R' Shimon Nezira: "If he made it into a compress, it is ritually pure," etc.

div.head: R' Shimon ben Nanas (a Tanna of the Mishnah) or simply Ben Nanas.
div.ab: ‫הלכותיו מצינו בכורים פ״ג מ״ט ר״ש בן ננס אומר מעטרין את הבכורים חוץ מז׳ המינים, רע״א אין מעטרין.

His halakhot are found in Bikkurim 3:9: "R' Shimon ben Nanas says: One may decorate the first-fruits with [anything] except the seven species; R' Akiva says: One may not decorate [them]" [except with the seven species].
ובשבת פ״טז מ״ה אמר פורסין עור וכו׳.
And in Shabbat 16:5 he said: "One may spread a hide, etc."
ובעירובין פ״י מ״טו מהיכן מוציאין אותו — דברי ר״ש בן ננס, ר״ע אומר וכו'.
And in Eruvin 10:15: "[The bolt] is removed from it [entirely] — the words of R' Shimon ben Nanas; R' Akiva says, etc."
ובכתובות פ״י מ״ה בן ננס אומר וכי מפני שהיא אחרונה נשכרת, אלא אף היא לא תפרע אלא בשבועה.
And in Ketubot 10:5: "Ben Nanas says: Is it because she is the last that she profits? Rather, she too may not collect except with an oath."
ובגיטין פ״ח מ״י גט קרח הכל משלימין עליו דברי בן ננס ורע״א וכו'.
And in Gittin 8:10: "A 'bald' bill of divorce, anyone may complete it — the words of Ben Nanas; and R' Akiva says, etc."
וב״ב פ״ז מ״ג מדה בחבל אני מוכר לך — דברי בן ננס. (ובאיכ״ר פ״א פ׳ ומרוב עבודה אמרו בההיא דתנן דברי בן ננס בסימניו ובמצריו, ונתחבר ע״פ טעות ב׳ משניות ביחד).

And in Bava Batra 7:3: "'[A field] measured by the rope I sell to you' — the words of Ben Nanas." (And in Eikhah Rabbah, chapter 1, on the verse "and from the abundance of servitude," they said regarding that which we learned in the Mishnah: "the words of Ben Nanas: 'by its signs and by its boundaries,'" and two mishnayot were mistakenly joined together).
ושם ספ״י ערב היוצא לאחר חיתום שטרות מעשה בא לפני ר' ישמעאל — ‫ א״ל בן ננס אינו גובה — א״ל למה? א״ל הרי החונק וכו', א״ר ישמעאל -‬ הרוצה שיעסוק בדיני ממונות ישמש את בן ננס.

And there at the end of chapter 10 [Bava Batra 10:8]: "A guarantor who appears below the signatures of the documents — a case came before R' Yishmael — Ben Nanas said to him: He collects nothing — He said to him: Why? He said to him: Behold, if one was strangling, etc. R' Yishmael said — One who wishes to engage in monetary laws should serve [as a disciple to] Ben Nanas."
ובשבועות פ״ז מ״ה הלכתו הנודע אמר בן ננס כיצד אלו ואלו באין לידי שבועת שוא אלא וכו'.
And in Shevuot 7:5 is his well-known halakhah: "Ben Nanas said: How could both these and those come to a vain oath? Rather, etc."
ובמנחות פ״ד מ״ג הלחם מעכב את הכבשים — דברי ר״ע, אר״ש בן ננס לא כי — אר״ש הלכה כבן ננס.
And in Menahot 4:3: "The bread is indispensable for the lambs — the words of R' Akiva; R' Shimon ben Nanas said: Not so — R' Shimon said: The halakhah is according to Ben Nanas."
וכן נזכר כתובות צ: מתו אחת בחייו‬ ‫— בן ננס אומר — רע״א כבר קפצה נחלה וכו'.
And likewise he is mentioned in Ketubot 90b: "If they died, one in his lifetime — Ben Nanas says — R' Akiva says: The inheritance has already leaped, etc."
ובספרא אמור אר״ע מי מכריע א״ל בן ננס אני אכריע.
And in Sifra, Emor: "R' Akiva said: Who will decide [between the opinions]? Ben Nanas said to him: I will decide."
ובתוספתא סוף מקואות מחלוקת ר״ע ורי״הג, סייע בן ננס לר״ע.
And in the Tosefta, at the end of Mikvaot, in a dispute between R' Akiva and R' Yose ha-Gelili, Ben Nanas supported R' Akiva.
ובשמחות פ״יב מחלוקת ר״ע ושמעון בן ננס.
And in Semahot, chapter 12, there is a dispute between R' Akiva and Shimon ben Nanas.

ודעת הרמ״בם בהקדמתו לזרעים שהוא מהחמשה הדנין לפני חכמים הנזכרין בסנהדרין יז:, וכן הוא שם בפי׳ ר״ח, אבל רש״י מפרש שהוא שמעון התימני, והצדק אתו כי מכל המקומות שהבאנו לעיל משמע שהיה כמו חבר לר״ע ולר' ישמעאל ולא תלמידם.

And the opinion of the Rambam in his Introduction to Zeraim is that he is one of the five "who argue before the Sages" mentioned in Sanhedrin 17b, and so it is there in the commentary of Rabbenu Hananel; however, Rashi explains that it is Shimon ha-Timni, and justice is with him, for from all the places that we have brought above it is implied that he was like a colleague to R' Akiva and to R' Yishmael, and not their disciple.
ולא נמצא שום דבר מחייו הפרטי.
And nothing of his private life is found.

div.head: Shimon bar Narshaya.
div.ab: ‫בירושלמי כלאים פ״ג סה״א ר׳ אבא בר כהנא שמעון בר נרשייה בשם רש״בל, ושם סה״ד המאמר בשם שמעון גרשייה, וקרוב לומר שהוא שם מקום.

In Yerushalmi Kilayim 3, end of halakhah 1: "R' Abba bar Kahana [and] Shimon bar Narshaya in the name of Resh Lakish"; and there at the end of halakhah 4, the statement is in the name of "Shimon Garshaya"; and it is likely to say that it is the name of a place.

div.head: R' Shimon ben Netanel.
div.ab: הוא היה תלמיד הרביעי מחמשה תלמידיו הגדולים דרבי יוחנן בן זכאי, כאבות פ״ב מ״ח, ורבו אמר עליו שהוא ירא שמים, וכשאמר להם צאו וראו איזהו דרך ישרה שיבור לו האדם אמר ר״ש בן נתנאל הרואה את הנולד, ואיזהו

He was the fourth disciple among the five great disciples of R' Yoḥanan ben Zakkai, as in Avot 2:8, and his teacher said of him that he was a fearer of Heaven. And when he said to them, "Go out and see which is the straight path that a person should choose for himself," R' Shimon ben Netanel said, "One who foresees the consequences." And [when he asked,] "Which is
דרך רעה שיתרחק ממנה האדם אמר הלוה ואינו משלם וכו'.
the evil path from which a person should distance himself," he said, "One who borrows and does not repay, etc."
ונשאר לנו ממנו מאמרו היקר שם מ״יג הוי זהיר בק״ש ובתפלה, וכשאתה מתפלל אל תעש תפלתך קבע אלא רחמים — ואל תהי רשע בפני עצמך.

And there remains to us from him his precious saying there, mishnah 13: "Be careful in the recitation of Shema and in prayer, and when you pray, do not make your prayer a fixed routine, rather [a plea for] mercy — and do not be wicked in your own eyes."

ובירושלמי חגיגה פ"ב ה"א שרי"בז ותלמידיו הלכו בדרך ור"א בן ערך דרש במעשה מרכבה וכיון ששמעו ר' יוסף הכהן ור״ש בן נתנאל אף הם פתחו במעשה מרכבה — ויצתה ב״ק וא"ל הרי המקום פנוי לכם והטרקלין מוצע לכם אתם ותלמידיכם מזומנין לכת שלישית, ובחגיגה יד. מובא המעשה ושם הגרסא ר׳ יהושע ולא ר״ש בן נתנאל.

And in Yerushalmi Ḥagigah 2:1, [it is related] that R' Yoḥanan ben Zakkai and his disciples were walking on the road, and R' Elazar ben Arakh expounded the Account of the Chariot, and when R' Yosef ha-Kohen and R' Shimon ben Netanel heard, they too began [to expound] the Account of the Chariot — and a heavenly voice went forth and said to them, "Behold, the place is cleared for you and the dining hall is spread out for you; you and your disciples are designated for the third class." And in Ḥagigah 14a the incident is brought, and there the reading is R' Yehoshua and not R' Shimon ben Netanel.
ומצינו בתוספתא ע״ז פ״ג מעשת בר״ג הזקן שהשיא את בתו לשמעון בן נתנאל הכהן ופסק עמו ע״מ שלא תעשה טהרות על גביו.

And we find in Tosefta Avodah Zarah chapter 3 an incident concerning Rabban Gamliel the Elder, that he married his daughter to Shimon ben Netanel ha-Kohen and stipulated with him on condition that she would not prepare pure things in reliance on him.

div.head: R' Shimon b. R' Simon.
div.ab: נזכר מד׳ תהלים פ״כה־ב, אך הוא ט״ס וצ״ל ר׳ סימון בשם ר׳ שמעון חסידא כמבואר בערכו.
He is mentioned in Midrash Tehillim 25:2, but it is a scribal error and one must read R' Simon in the name of R' Shimon Ḥasida, as explained in his entry.

div.head: Shimon ben Azzai, or simply by the name Ben Azzai
div.ab: הוא נזכר הרבה יותר במשנה מחבירו בן זומא.
He is mentioned much more in the Mishnah than his colleague Ben Zoma.
בברכות פ״ט מ״ד בן עזאי אומר (הנכנס לכרך) מתפלל ד', ב' בכניסתו וב׳ ביציאתו.
In Berakhot, chapter 9, mishnah 4: Ben Azzai says, (one who enters a fortified city) prays four [prayers], two upon his entry and two upon his exit.
ובשקלים רפ״ג חולק על ר״ע באיזה זמן תורמין את הלשכה.
And in Shekalim, start of chapter 3, he disagrees with R' Akiva regarding at what time they appropriate the terumah of the chamber.
ושם פ״ד מ״ו א"ל בן עזאי לר"ע אינה היא המדה.
And there, chapter 4, mishnah 6: Ben Azzai said to R' Akiva, "That is not the rule."
ושם פ״ה מ"ג ה׳ חותמות היו במקדש.
And there, chapter 5, mishnah 3: "There were five seals in the Temple."

וביומא פ״ב מ״ג אמר בן עזאי לפני ר״ע משום ר' יהושע דרך הלוכו היה קרב. ובתענית פ״ד מ״ד א״ל ב״ע לר״ע כך היה ר׳ יהושע שונה קרבן מוסף — חזר בו ר״ע להיות שונה כב״ע. ‫ וביבמות פ״ד מ״יג א״ר שמעון ב"ע מצאתי מגילת יוחסין בירושלים וכתוב בה איש פלוני ממזר מא"א לקיים דברי ר' יהושע, (ובגמרא שם מט: תני שמעון ב"עא מצאתי מגילת יוחסין בירושלים וכתוב בה איש פלוני ממזר מא"א, וכתוב בה משנת רא"בי קב ונקי, ‬וכתוב בה מנשה הרג את ישעיה).

And in Yoma, chapter 2, mishnah 3: Ben Azzai said before R' Akiva in the name of R' Yehoshua, "It was offered in the manner of its walking." And in Ta'anit, chapter 4, mishnah 4: Ben Azzai said to R' Akiva, "Thus R' Yehoshua used to teach [regarding] the musaf offering" — R' Akiva retracted to teach like Ben Azzai. And in Yevamot, chapter 4, mishnah 13: R' Shimon ben Azzai said, "I found a scroll of genealogies in Jerusalem, and it was written in it: 'So-and-so is a mamzer from a married woman,' to confirm the words of R' Yehoshua" (and in the Gemara there, 49b: Shimon ben Azzai taught: "I found a scroll of genealogies in Jerusalem, and it was written in it: 'So-and-so is a mamzer from a married woman,' and it was written in it: 'The Mishnah of R' Eliezer ben Yaakov is a kav and pure,' and it was written in it: 'Menasheh killed Isaiah'").
ובסוטה פ״ג מ״ד מכאן אמר ב״ע חייב ‫אדם ללמד את בתו תורה שאם תשתה תדע שהזכות תולה לה (וחולק בזה על ר״א ור' יהושע).

And in Sotah, chapter 3, mishnah 4: "From here Ben Azzai said: A person is obligated to teach his daughter Torah, so that if she drinks [the bitter water] she will know that merit suspends [the punishment] for her" (and in this he disagrees with R' Eliezer and R' Yehoshua).
וב״ב פ״ט מ״י א״ל ב״ע לר״ע על החלוקין אנו מצטערין אלא שבאת לחלוק עלינו את השוין.
And in Bava Batra, chapter 9, mishnah 10: Ben Azzai said to R' Akiva, "Even over the matters in dispute we are distressed; rather, you have come to divide for us the matters on which they agree!"
ובהוריות פ"א מ"ב א"ל ב"ע לר"ע מ"ש זה מן היושב בביתו.
And in Horayot, chapter 1, mishnah 2: Ben Azzai said to R' Akiva, "How does this one differ from one who sits in his house?"
ובזבחים פ״א מ״ב אמר שמעון ב״ע מקובל אני מפי עב' זקן ביום שהושיבו את רא"בע בישיבה שכל הזבחים - ולא הוסיף ב"ע אלא העולה ולא הודו לו חכמים.

And in Zevaḥim, chapter 1, mishnah 2: Shimon ben Azzai said, "I have received a tradition from the mouths of seventy-two elders on the day that they seated R' Elazar ben Azaryah in the academy, that all sacrifices..." — and Ben Azzai did not add anything except the burnt-offering, and the Sages did not agree with him.
וכן ידים פ"ג מ"ה אר"ש בן עזאי מקובל אני מפי עב' זקן - שש"הש וקהלת מטמאין את הידים, אר"ע חו"ש - א"ר יוחנן בן יהושע בן חמיו של ר"ע כדברי ב"ע כך נחלקו.

And likewise Yadayim, chapter 3, mishnah 5: R' Shimon ben Azzai said, "I have received a tradition from the mouths of seventy-two elders... that Song of Songs and Kohelet render the hands impure." R' Akiva said, "Heaven forbid!..." R' Yoḥanan ben Yehoshua, the son of R' Akiva's father-in-law, said, "In accordance with the words of Ben Azzai, so they disputed."
ובכורות פ"ט מ"ה חולק על ר"ע באיזה זמן תורמין מעשר בהמה.
And in Bekhorot, chapter 9, mishnah 5, he disagrees with R' Akiva regarding at what time they separate animal tithe.
ובקנים פ״ב מ״ה בן עזאי אומר הולכין אחר הראשון,
And in Kinnim, chapter 2, mishnah 5: Ben Azzai says, "We follow the first."
ושם פ״ג מ״ו בן עזאי אומר ב' חטאות.
And there, chapter 3, mishnah 6: Ben Azzai says, "Two sin-offerings."
ובפרה רפ"א אמר ר׳ יהושע — כך שמעתי סתם אמר בן עזאי אני אפרש.
And in Parah, start of chapter 1: R' Yehoshua said, "...Thus I heard without specification." Ben Azzai said, "I will explain."
ושם מ״ג ר״ט קורהו פלגס, ‬בן עזאי קורהו נוקד, ר׳ ישמעאל קורהו וכו׳.
And there, mishnah 3: R' Tarfon calls it palgas, Ben Azzai calls it noked, R' Yishmael calls it, etc.
ובנדה פ"ה מ״ח איזהו סימניה ריהג״א ‫— רע״א — בן עזאי אומר משישחירו הפיטומת.
And in Niddah, chapter 5, mishnah 8: "What are its signs? R' Yose ha-Gelili says... R' Akiva says... Ben Azzai says: From when the nipples blacken."
רבותיו נראה שהיו ר׳ יהושע כיומא פ״ב מ״ג, תענית פ״ב מ״ד שאמר לר״ע משום ר' יהושע או כך היה ר' יהושע שונה.

His teachers appear to have been R' Yehoshua, as in Yoma, chapter 2, mishnah 3, [and] Ta'anit, chapter 2 [4], mishnah 4, where he said to R' Akiva in the name of R' Yehoshua, or "Thus R' Yehoshua used to teach."
‫וביבמות פ״ד מ״יג מביא לקיים דברי‬ ר' יהושע.
And in Yevamot, chapter 4, mishnah 13, he brings [a proof] to confirm the words of R' Yehoshua.
ובפרה רפ״א ותוספתא שביעית פ״ב מפרש דברי ר' יהושע.
And in Parah, start of chapter 1, and Tosefta Shevi'it, chapter 2, he explains the words of R' Yehoshua.
אבל רבו המובהק היה ר׳ עקיבא כב״ב קנח: במשנה שאמר בן עזאי לר״ע על החלוקין אנו מצטערין אלא שבאת לחלק עלינו את השוין, א״ר שמלאי עדא אמרה, בן עזאי תלמיד חבר דר״ע הוה דקאמר ליה ״שבאת״,

However, his primary teacher was R' Akiva, as in Bava Batra 158b: regarding the mishnah where Ben Azzai said to R' Akiva, "Even over the matters in dispute we are distressed; rather, you have come to divide for us the matters on which they agree," R' Simlai said: "This implies that Ben Azzai was a disciple-colleague of R' Akiva, since he said to him 'that you have come.'"

ופי׳ הרש״בם דמתחלה היה תלמידו ולבסוף היה חבירו, ובפי׳ רבינו גרשום שהלכו שניהם ללמוד תורה לפני ר׳ אליעזר הגדול, ולפי שהיה בן עזאי בחור לא היה יכול לסבול סברא כר״ע בתלמוד וגמר גמרא והדר הלך בן עזאי לפני ר״ע להסביר סברא, ונראה שנפל טעות בדבריו הקדושים וצ״ל שהלכו לפני ר׳ יהושע כדמובא לעיל שאמר בשמו אבל לא מצינו בשום מקום שיאמר בשם ר״א אבל ר״ע היה באמת רבו המובהק כברכות סב‪ .‬שאמר בן עזאי פ״א נכנסתי אחר ר״ע לבה״כ ולמדתי ממנו ג׳ דברים — א״ל ר׳ יהודה עד כאן העזת פניך ברבך? ואף שר״ע היה רבו המובהק דרבי יהודה ג״כ, אך זה כמו שאמר שם בן בן עזאי אומר עזאי לר״ע עד כאן העזת פניך ״ברבך״ ר' יהושע ואף שר״י היה גם רבו דבן עזאי, אך הלשון הזה אינו לומר שהיה אך רבו דר״ע, אבל הכונה שא״ל הלא הוא רבך ואיך העזת פניך לעשות כן.

And Rashbam explained that at first he was his disciple and in the end he was his colleague. And in the commentary of Rabbenu Gershom: that the two of them went to study Torah before R' Eliezer ha-Gadol, and because Ben Azzai was a young man he was unable to grasp logical reasoning like R' Akiva in Talmud, so he learned the traditions, and afterward Ben Azzai went before R' Akiva to explain the logical reasoning. And it seems that an error fell into his holy words, and one must read that they went before R' Yehoshua, as brought above that he said [traditions] in his name, whereas we do not find in any place that he says [anything] in the name of R' Eliezer. However, R' Akiva was in truth his primary teacher, as in Berakhot 62a, where Ben Azzai said: "Once I entered after R' Akiva into the privy and I learned from him three things..." R' Yehudah said to him, "Up to this point did you act so brazenly toward your teacher?" And even though R' Akiva was the primary teacher of R' Yehudah also, nevertheless this is like what Ben Azzai said there — [where the text reads "Ben Azzai says," i.e., Ben] Azzai to R' Akiva: "Up to this point did you act so brazenly toward 'your teacher'" R' Yehoshua; and even though R' Yehoshua was also the teacher of Ben Azzai, yet this expression does not mean to say that he was only the teacher of R' Akiva, rather the intention is that he said to him: "Is he not your teacher, and how did you act so brazenly to do thus?"
וכן מכלתא בא פ״א וספרא ויקרא פ״ב אר״ש בן עזאי איני כמשיכ על דברי רבי (ר׳ עקיבא) אלא כמוסיף על דבריו.

And likewise Mekhilta, Bo, chapter 1, and Sifra, Vayikra, chapter 2: R' Shimon ben Azzai said, "I am not like one who refutes the words of my teacher (R' Akiva), but rather like one who adds to his words."
וברכות כב. ר״ע לחשה לבן עזאי וכו'. וכשהיה אצל ר״ע אמרו כתובות סג. ברתיה דר״ע עבדה לבן עזאי הכי (שנתקדשה לו בצנעה ע״מ שילך ללמוד) והיינו דאמרי אינשי רחילא בתר רחילא אזלא כעובדי אמה כך עובדי ברתה.

And Berakhot 22a: "R' Akiva whispered it to Ben Azzai, etc." And when he was with R' Akiva, they said [in] Ketubot 63a: "The daughter of R' Akiva did thus to Ben Azzai" (that she became betrothed to him in secret on condition that he go to study), "and this is what people say: 'Ewe follows ewe; as the deeds of the mother, so are the deeds of her daughter.'"

ובסוטה ד: אמדו אב״א נסיב ופירש, ובל״ס יען שהיה שקדן גדול בתורה וגם נכנס לפרדס וכאשר נבאר לקמן לכן פירש לגמרי מדרכי ע״הז, וכדאמרו יבמות סג: כשדרש כל שאינו עוסק בפ״ור כאלו שופך דמים וממעט הדמות אמרו לו — אתה נאה דורש ואינו נאה מקיים א״ל ומה אעשה שנפשי חשקה בתורה אפשר לעולם שיתקיים ע״י אחרים, וכפי הנראה כשגירש את בת ר״ע רבו פירש אז ממנו ואח״כ התאונן ע״ז כנדרים עד: שאמר חבל עלך בן עזאי שלא שימשת (יותר) את ר״ע.

And in Sotah 4b they said: "If you wish, say: he married and separated." And without doubt, because he was a great diligent student in Torah and also entered the Pardes, as we shall explain below, he therefore separated completely from the ways of this world. And as they said [in] Yevamot 63b: when he expounded, "Anyone who does not engage in being fruitful and multiplying is as though he sheds blood and diminishes the [Divine] image," they said to him, "...You expound well, but you do not fulfill well!" He said to them, "And what shall I do, for my soul craves Torah; it is possible for the world to be sustained through others." And as it appears, when he divorced the daughter of R' Akiva his teacher, he then separated from him, and afterward he lamented over this, as in Nedarim 74b, where he said: "Alas for you, Ben Azzai, that you did not attend (more) upon R' Akiva!"
וכן התאונן שלא שימש את ר' ישמעאל כחולין ע: עא.
And likewise he lamented that he did not attend upon R' Yishmael, as in Ḥullin 70b–71a.
והכיר תמיד גדולת רבו ר״ע אף ‫כשהגדיל יותר מכל חכמי דורו ואמר בכורות נח. כל חכמי ישראל דומין עלי כקליפת השום חוץ מן הקרח הזה (הוא ר״ע, רש״י).

And he always recognized the greatness of his teacher R' Akiva, even when he grew greater than all the sages of his generation and said [in] Bekhorot 58a: "All the sages of Israel seem to me like the peel of garlic, except for this bald one" (that is R' Akiva — Rashi).
הוא היה מהר' הנקראין בשם ״דנין לפני חכמים״ שמעון בן עזאי ושמעון בן זומא וחנן המצרי וחנניה בן חכינאי כסנהדרין יז:, ואמרו הוריות ב: ראוי להוראה כגון מאן אמר רבא כגון שמעון בן עזאי ושמעון ב״ז.

He was one of the four who are called by the title "those who argue before the Sages": Shimon ben Azzai, and Shimon ben Zoma, and Ḥanan the Egyptian, and Ḥananyah ben Ḥakhinai, as in Sanhedrin 17b. And they said [in] Horayot 2b: "'Fit to issue a halakhic ruling' — like whom? Rava said: Like Shimon ben Azzai and Shimon ben Zoma."
ובקידושין מט: ע״מ שאני תלמיד אין אומרים כשמעון בן עזאי וכשמעון ב״ז (תלמידים היו ובחורים ולא באו לכלל סמיכה ולא היה בימיהם כמותם בתורה, רש״י).

And in Kiddushin 49b: "'On condition that I am a Torah scholar (talmid)' — we do not say like Shimon ben Azzai and like Shimon ben Zoma" (they were disciples and unmarried young men, and did not reach the status of ordination, and there was none in their days like them in Torah — Rashi).
הלכותיו בברייתא מצינו ברכות כא: ‫שדרש סמוכין שמכשפה בסקילה.
His halakhot in the Baraita we find [in] Berakhot 21b, that he expounded juxtaposed verses [to teach] that a sorceress is [executed] by stoning.
ובה: מהלך כעומד דמי, המוציא והמכניס פטור, המושיט והזורק חייב.
And in Shabbat 5b: "Walking is like standing: one who carries out and one who brings in is exempt; one who passes [an object across] and one who throws is liable."
ובר״ה ו. אותו בלא ירצה ולא מאחר נדרו בלא ירצה.
And in Rosh Hashanah 6a: "'It' falls under [the transgression of] 'it shall not be accepted,' and one who delays his vow does not fall under 'it shall not be accepted.'"
וביבמות נא: יש מאמר אחר מאמר בשני יבמין.
And in Yevamot 51b: "There is validity to a levirate betrothal (ma'amar) after a levirate betrothal with two yevamin."
‫ובסוטה‬ כמה שיעור סתירה כדי לצלות ביצה (וחולק שם עם ר״א ור׳ יהושע ור׳ ישמעאל ור״ע).
And in Sotah [4a]: "How much is the measure of seclusion? Enough to roast an egg" (and he disagrees there with R' Eliezer, and R' Yehoshua, and R' Yishmael, and R' Akiva).
ובקידושין כה‪ .‬רבי אומר אף הסירוס‪,‬‬ ‫בן עזאי אומר אף הלשון (ואמרו שם בגמרא‬ ‫שלכן סידרו דברי דבי בהחלה חנא שמעה לדרבי‬ ‫וקבעה‪ ,‬ושמעה לדבן עזאי ותני‪ ,‬ומשנה לא זזה‬ ‫ממקומה).

The Hebrew of this paragraph on Wikisource is uncorrected OCR (columns mixed, letters confused). The translation is not reliable; read the scan. And in Kiddushin 25a: "R' Yehuda HaNasi says: Even castration; Ben Azzai says: Even the tongue" (and they said there in the Gemara that the reason they arranged the words of R' Yehuda HaNasi at the beginning is that the Tanna heard that of R' Yehuda HaNasi and established it, and heard that of Ben Azzai and taught it, and the Mishnah did not move from its place).
וכן ב״ק פד: רבי אומר כויה נאמרה תחלה בן עזאי אומר חבורה נאמרה תחלה.
And likewise Bava Kamma 84b: "R' Yehuda HaNasi says: 'Burning' was stated first; Ben Azzai says: 'Wounding' was stated first."
ושם קה. אמר ג׳ שבועות הן.
And there, 105a, he said: "There are three oaths."
וכן נזכר מכלתא בא פ״יח, בשלח פ״א, משפטים פ״י.
And likewise he is mentioned [in] Mekhilta, Bo, chapter 18; Beshallaḥ, chapter 1; Mishpatim, chapter 10.
דבריו היקרים באגדה מצינו אבות ‫פ״ד מ״ב ג׳‪ ,‬הוי רץ למצוה קלה כבחמורה ובורח מן העבירה שמצוה גוררת מצוה — אל תהי בז לכל אדם ואל תהי מפליג לכל דבר, שאין לך אדם שאין לו שעה, ואין לך דבר שאין לו מקום.

His precious words in Aggadah we find [in] Avot, chapter 4, mishnah 2 [and] 3: "Run to a minor mitzvah as to a major one, and flee from a transgression; for a mitzvah draws a mitzvah... Do not despise any person, and do not push aside any thing, for you have no person who does not have his hour, and you have no thing that does not have its place."

ובאדר״נ ספ״כה אמר רד ממקומך ב' וג׳ מעלות ושב, טוב שיאמרו לך עלה משיאמרו לך רד, ואמר נוח למלוך על כל העולם מלישב ולשנות בפני בני אדם העטופים בסדינין (למי שאין תוכו כברו), והמאמר מובא בויק״ר פ״א־ה ושם ר״ע בשם ר״ש בן עזאי והוא ט״ס וצ״ל ר״ע ואית דמתני לה בשם רש״בע.

And in Avot de-Rabbi Natan, end of chapter 25, he said: "Descend from your place two or three levels and sit; it is better that they say to you 'Go up' than that they say to you 'Go down.'" And he said: "It is easier to rule over the entire world than to sit and teach before people who are wrapped in linen sheets" (referring to one whose inside is not like his outside). And the statement is brought in Vayikra Rabbah 1:5, and there [it reads] R' Akiva in the name of R' Shimon ben Azzai, and it is a scribal error and one must read: R' Akiva, and there are those who teach it in the name of R' Shimon ben Azzai.
וברכות ו: אמר מאי כי זה כל האדם שכל העולם כולו לא נברא אלא לצוות לזה (למי שיש בו יראת שמים).

And [in] Berakhot 6b he said: "What is [the meaning of] 'for this is the whole of man'? That the entire world was created only to keep company with this one" (for one who has the fear of Heaven in him).
ושם מז. כל המאריך‬ באמן מאריכין לו ימיו ושנותיו.
And there, 47a: "Anyone who prolongs 'Amen,' they prolong his days and his years for him."
ושם מז: איזהו ע״ה כל שאין לו ציצית בבגדו.
And there, 47b: "Who is an am ha-aretz? Anyone who does not have tzitzit on his garment."

וביומא לח. אמר בשמך יקראוך ובמקומך יושיבוך ומשלך יתנו לך, אין אדם נוגע במוכן לחבירו ואין מלכות נוגעת בחברתה אפילו כמלא נימא (ואפשר שאמר זאת יען שמפני איזה סיבה לא נסמך ולכן אמר שאין לו להצטער ע״ז יען שכן הוא גזירה מן השמים והכל בהשגחה).

And in Yoma 38a he said: "By your name they will call you, and in your place they will seat you, and from what is yours they will give you; no person touches what is prepared for his fellow, and no kingdom touches its fellow even as much as a hair's breadth" (and it is possible that he said this because for some reason he was not ordained, and therefore he said that he should not be distressed over this, because so it is a decree from Heaven and everything is by Divine providence).
ובמגילה יג. אמר אסתר לא ארוכה ולא קצרה היתה אלא בינונית כהדסה.
And in Megillah 13a he said: "Esther was neither tall nor short, but rather of medium height, like a myrtle (hadassah)."
ומאמרו היקר מנחות קי. אחד המרבה ואחד הממעיט ובלבד שיכוון לבו לשמים.
And his precious statement [in] Menaḥot 110a: "It is all one whether a person offers much or offers little, provided that he directs his heart to Heaven."
ובתו״כ קדושימ פ' ואהבת לרעך כמוך רע״א זה כלל גדול בתורה, בן עזאי אומר זה ספר תולדות אדם, זה כלל גדול מזה, וכן הוא בירושלמי נדרים ‫פ״ט ה״ג.

And in Torat Kohanim, Kedoshim, on the verse "And you shall love your neighbor as yourself": R' Akiva says, "This is a great principle in the Torah"; Ben Azzai says, "'This is the book of the generations of Adam' — this is a greater principle than that." And so it is in Yerushalmi Nedarim 9:3.
ובערכין טז: עד היכן היא תוכחה ואמר עד נזיפה (וחולק על ר״א ור׳ יהושע),
And in Arakhin 16b: "Up to what point is rebuke?" And he said: "Up to scolding" (and he disagrees with R' Eliezer and R' Yehoshua).
ויסופר ויק״ר פ״טז־ד שהיה יושב ודורש והאש מלהטת סביבותיו א״ל שמא בסדרי מרכבה אתה עוסק א״ל לאו אלא מחריז ד״ת לנביאים ונביאים לכתובים.

And it is told [in] Vayikra Rabbah 16:4 that he was sitting and expounding and fire was blazing around him. They said to him, "Perhaps you are engaging in the workings of the Chariot?" He said to them, "No, rather I am stringing words of Torah to the Prophets and the Prophets to the Writings."
וכן היה בקי בלשון יונית כסוכה לה. שאמר א״ת הדר אלא אדור שכן בלשון יוני וכו'.
And likewise he was an expert in the Greek language, as in Sukkah 35a, where he said: "Do not read hadar, but rather hudor, for in the Greek language, etc."
ובטבעיות כברכות סב: שאמר על כל משכב שכב חוץ מן הקרקע, על כל מושב שב חוץ מן הקורה, השכם והערב וצא.
And in natural health matters, as in Berakhot 62b, where he said: "Lie on any couch except the ground; sit on any seat except a beam; rise early and stay up late and go out [to relieve yourself]."
ור׳ יוסי הגלילי היה כמו חבירו כספרא מצורע־־קנב. שא״ל ריה״ג פרשה א״ל אין מפרשים לחכם, וחולק עמו נדרים עח., ב״ק יג.

And R' Yossi ha-Gelili was like his colleague, as in Sifra Metzora 152a, where R' Yossi ha-Gelili said to him: "Explain it!" He said to him: "One does not explain to a sage." And he disagrees with him in Nedarim 78a, Bava Kamma 13a.
‫מקומו הקבוע היה בטבריא כעירובין כט. שאמר רבא הריני כבן עזאי בשוקי טבריא. ובקידושין כ. אמר אביי כן.
His permanent place was in Tiberias, as in Eruvin 29a, where Rava said: "Behold, I am like Ben Azzai in the markets of Tiberias." And in Kiddushin 20a, Abaye said thus.
ובכורים פ״ב ה״ב התפאר ר׳ יוחנן (שהיה בטבריא) ואמר אנא בן עזאי דהכא.
And in Yerushalmi Bikkurim 2:2, R' Yoḥanan (who was in Tiberias) boasted and said: "I am the Ben Azzai of here."
והרביץ שם תורה הרבה עם תלמידים כברכות כב. שאמרו ר״ע לחשה לב״ע, ובן עזאי יצא ושנה לתלמידיו בשוק.

And he disseminated much Torah there with disciples, as in Berakhot 22a, where they said: "R' Akiva whispered it to Ben Azzai, and Ben Azzai went out and taught it to his disciples in the marketplace."
ואף שלא נזכרו בשמותם אבל מצינו שר' יוסי אמר בשמו כתמורה כא: א״ר יוסי ג׳ דברים משום ג׳ זקנים ר׳ ישמעאל ר״ע ובן עזאי.

And although they are not mentioned by their names, nevertheless we find that R' Yossi said in his name, as in Temurah 21b: R' Yossi said three things in the name of three elders, R' Yishmael, R' Akiva, and Ben Azzai.
ומה שמצינו ב״ק נט. ר׳ יוסי אומר נכי חיה, בן עזאי אומר נכי מזונות צ״ל שם ר״י הגלילי, וכן מה שאמרו נזיר סה. ר׳ יוחנן משום ב״ע הוא תנא דאמרו שם דתניא כמה שיעור תפיסה אר״י משום ב״ע וכו'.

And that which we find in Bava Kamma 59a: "R' Yossi says: Deduction is made for childbirth; Ben Azzai says: Deduction is made for sustenance"—one must read there R' Yossi ha-Gelili. And similarly, that which they said in Nazir 65a: "R' Yoḥanan in the name of Ben Azzai," it is a Tanna, for they said there: "As it was taught: What is the measure of earth that has been moved? R' Yoḥanan said in the name of Ben Azzai, etc."

והנה מלבד גדולתו בתורה היה עוסק גם בנסתרות במעשה מרכבה ומעשה בראשית בחגיגה יד: ד' נכנסו לפרדס בן עזאי, בן זומא, אחר ור״ע, ור״ע הזהירם וא״ל כשאתם מגיעין אצל אבני שיש טהור אל תאמרו מים מים אבל אך ר״ע נבנם בשלום ויצא בשלום, אבל בן עזאי הציץ ומת ועליו הכתוב אומר יקר בעיני ה׳ המותה לחסידיו, בן זומא הציץ ונפגע, ובירושלמי שם איתא להיפוך, ורש״י פירש שמת בחור, ולפי פשטות הגיע לימי זקנה כי בזמן חכמי יבנה היה כבר מגדולי הדור שהיה מהדנין לפני חכמים וחי עד שנתגדל רבי יהודה ודיבר אתו כדרך חברים כברכות סב. ‫יבמות ד..

Now, aside from his greatness in Torah, he also engaged in esoteric matters, in the Account of the Chariot and the Account of Creation, in Ḥagigah 14b: "Four entered the Pardes: Ben Azzai, Ben Zoma, Aḥer, and R' Akiva. And R' Akiva warned them and said to them: 'When you arrive at the stones of pure marble, do not say: Water, water!'" However, only R' Akiva entered in peace and departed in peace, whereas Ben Azzai gazed and died, and regarding him Scripture says: "Precious in the eyes of the Lord is the death of His pious ones"; Ben Zoma gazed and was stricken. And in the Yerushalmi there it is found the reverse. And Rashi explained that he died as a young man, capability [?], but according to the plain sense he reached old age, for in the time of the sages of Yavneh he was already among the great men of the generation, as he was among those who argued before the sages, and he lived until R' Yehuda grew up and spoke with him in the manner of colleagues, as in Berakhot 62a, Yevamot 4a.
וכן ר׳ יונתן שידוע ששימש את ר׳ ישמעאל בסוף ימיו מצינו חולין ז: א״ר יונתן נמתי לו לבן עזאי — נם לי ומה ‬ישמעאל אומר וכו'.
And similarly R' Yonatan, who it is known served R' Yishmael at the end of his days, we find in Ḥullin 70b: R' Yonatan said: "I said to Ben Azzai... He said to me: And what does Yishmael say, etc."

‫ודעת המדרש תהלים פ״ט־יג ואיכ״ר פ״ב פ' בלע שבן עזאי היה מהרוגי מלכות, אבל בגמרא שלנו מפורש סוטה פ״ט מ״טו משמת בן עזאי בטלו השקדנין משמע שנפטר כדרך כל הארץ, וכן מה שאמרו בחגיגה יד: בן עזאי הציץ ומת משמע כן,

And the opinion of Midrash Tehillim 9:13 and Eikha Rabbah, chapter 2, on the verse "The Lord has swallowed up" [2:2], is that Ben Azzai was among the martyrs of the [Roman] government. However, in our Gemara it is explicit, Sotah chapter 9, mishnah 15: "When Ben Azzai died, the diligent students ceased," which implies that he passed away in the way of all the earth; and similarly that which they said in Ḥagigah 14b: "Ben Azzai gazed and died" implies thus.
ואמרו עליו ברכות נז: הרואה בן עזאי בחלום יצפה לחסידות.
And they said about him in Berakhot 57b: "One who sees Ben Azzai in a dream may expect piety."

div.head: R' Shimon ben R' Akiva.
div.ab: בירושלמי ברכות ספ״ו מעשה בר״ע שעשה משתה לשמעון בנו ועל כל חבית — אמר חמרא טבא וכו', ובשבת סז. מובא המעשה אך לא נזכר שם בנו.

In Yerushalmi Berakhot, end of chapter 6: "An incident concerning R' Akiva, who made a feast for his son Shimon, and over every barrel — he said: 'Good wine,' etc." And in Shabbat 67a the incident is brought, but the name of his son is not mentioned.
אך בנו היקר מת בחייו בשמחות פ״ח כשהיה ר' שמעון בנו של ר״ע חולה לא ביטל בית מדרשו וכשמת הספידו אביו ואמר יודע אני שהוא בן ע״הב שזיכה את הרבים.

However, his dear son died in his lifetime. In Semahot chapter 8: "When R' Shimon the son of R' Akiva was ill, he [R' Akiva] did not suspend his study hall, and when he died, his father eulogized him and said: 'I know that he is a son of the World to Come, for he brought merit to the public.'"

div.head: R' Shimon b. Akashya.
div.ab: נשאר לנו ממנו מאמרו היקר במשנה סוף קנים שאמר זקני ע״ה כ״ז שמזקינן דעתן מטורפת עליהן — אבל זקני תורה אינו כן אלא כ״ז שמזקינן דעתן מתישבת‬ עליהן.

There remains to us from him his precious statement in the Mishnah at the end of Kinnim, where he said: "The elders of the unlearned, as long as they grow old, their minds become confused — but the elders of Torah, it is not so; rather, as long as they grow old, their minds become settled."

div.head: R' Shimon ben Pazi.
div.ab: הנה דעת התוס׳ ב״ב קמט. ד״ה רב מרי שפזי הוא שם אשה בת ר' חייא כיבמות סה:, וכן מובא בהר"ש סוף אהלות. אבל מצינו מנילה יג. (לגרסת ע"י ודק״ס) אר״ש בן פזי כי הוה פתח ״אבא פזי״ ברה״י וכו', ובערכין טז: בעא מיניה‬ ר״ש בן פזי מר׳ פזי תוכחה לשמה וכו׳ ‫(לגרסת שיטה מקובצת), ומזה אנו רואין בבירור שהוא שם איש.

Now, the opinion of Tosafot in Bava Batra 149a, s.v. "Rav Mari", is that Pazi is the name of a woman, the daughter of R' Ḥiyya, as in Yevamot 65b, and so it is brought in the commentary of R' Shimshon of Sens at the end of Ohalot. However, we find in Megillah 13a (according to the reading of Ein Yaakov and Dikdukei Soferim): R' Shimon ben Pazi said, "When 'my father Pazi' would open [his discourse] on the Book of Chronicles, etc." And in Arakhin 16b: R' Shimon ben Pazi inquired of R' Pazi, "Rebuke for the sake of Heaven, etc." (according to the reading of Shitah Mekubetzet). From this we see clearly that it is the name of a man.

וכבר בארתי בערך ר' יהודה בריה דר״ש בן פזי שאבי המשפחה ר׳ פזי היה דר בעיר לוד והיה עוד בזמן רבי‪ ,‬ובנו ר׳ שמעון היה תלמיד מובהק לרי״בל שהיה ג״כ בלוד וכדמצינו תמיד אר״ש בן פזי ארי״בל כברכות לד., שבת מ. עה. קה: קיח., פסחים כו., סוכה לח: מגילה יג., ביצה יד: כז., מו״ק ג:, נדרים עו: פז., ע״ז לה..

And I have already explained in the entry on R' Yehuda the son of R' Shimon ben Pazi that the patriarch of the family, R' Pazi, lived in the city of Lod and was still [alive] in the time of R' Yehuda HaNasi, and his son R' Shimon was a primary disciple of R' Yehoshua ben Levi, who was also in Lod, as we always find: "R' Shimon ben Pazi said that R' Yehoshua ben Levi said," as in Berakhot 34a; Shabbat 40a, 75a, 105b, 118a; Pesaḥim 26a; Sukkah 38b; Megillah 13a; Beitzah 14b, 27a; Moed Katan 3b; Nedarim 76b, 87a; Avodah Zarah 35a.
וכן כתובות נז. כי אתא רב דימי‬ אר״ש בן פזי ארי״בל, ושם נז. קד: כי אתא רבין אר״ש בן פזי ארי״בל.

And similarly in Ketubot 57a: "When Rav Dimi came [to Babylonia], he said that R' Shimon ben Pazi said that R' Yehoshua ben Levi said"; and there on 57a [and] 104b: "When Ravin came [to Babylonia], he said that R' Shimon ben Pazi said that R' Yehoshua ben Levi said."
וקבל מריב״ל דרכי אגדה כברכות י. שאמרו רב שימי בר עוקבא ואמרי לה מר עוקבא (אין זה מר עוקבא ריש גלותא) הוה שכיח קמיה דר״ש בן פזי והוה מסדר (ר״ש בן פזי) אגדתא קמיה דרי״בל.

And he received from R' Yehoshua ben Levi the methods of aggadah, as in Berakhot 10a, where they said: Rav Shimi bar Ukva, and some say Mar Ukva (this is not Mar Ukva the Exilarch), was frequently before R' Shimon ben Pazi, and he (R' Shimon ben Pazi) would arrange aggadahs before R' Yehoshua ben Levi.
וכן מצינו שאמר בשם בר קפרא (שהיה ג״כ בררום) בזבחים סא:.
And similarly we find that he spoke in the name of Bar Kappara (who was also in the South [of Eretz Yisrael]) in Zevaḥim 61b.
וכל דבריו מצינו אך באגדה והיה בקי גדול במקרא כברכות מה. שאמר מנין שאין המתרגם רשאי להגביה קולו יותר מן הקורא שנאמר וכו'. ושם סא. וייצר אוי לי מיוצרי ואוי לי מיצרי.

And all of his statements are found only in aggadah, and he was a great expert in Scripture, as in Berakhot 45a, where he said: "From where [do we know] that the translator is not permitted to raise his voice louder than the reader? For it is said, etc." And there on 61a: "['And the Lord God] formed (vayyitzer)' [written with two yods]—'Woe to me from my Creator (yotzri), and woe to me from my [evil] inclination (yitzri).'"
ומו״ק ה. רמז לציון קברות מן התורה מנין ת״ל וכו'.
And in Moed Katan 5a: "From where is there an allusion in the Torah to the marking of graves? The verse teaches, etc."
וביבמות יג. מ״ט דב״ש דכתיב לא תהיה אשת המת וכו'.
And in Yevamot 13a: "What is the reason of Beit Shammai? Because it is written: 'The wife of the dead shall not be, etc.'"
ובסוטה מא: דרש שמותר להחניף לרשעים בע״הז שנאמר וכו'.
And in Sotah 41b he expounded that "it is permitted to flatter the wicked in this world, for it is said, etc."
‫ובע״ז יח: דרש הפסוק אשרי האיש.
And in Avodah Zarah 18b he expounded the verse "Praiseworthy is the man."
חבריו היו ר' אבהו ור׳ יצחק נפחא כביצה לח., ור׳ יצחק בר נחמני שחולקין תמיד כמגילה כג., סנהדרין י:, שבועות טז:, ור״נ בר יצחק נתן כלל שכ״מ שמצינו (סתם) שמעון הוא ר״ש בן פזי,

His colleagues were R' Abbahu and R' Yitzḥak Nappaḥa, as in Beitzah 38a, and R' Yitzḥak bar Naḥmani, who always dispute, as in Megillah 23a, Sanhedrin 10b, [and] Shevuot 16b; and Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak gave a rule that wherever we find an (unspecified) Shimon [there], it is R' Shimon ben Pazi,
והניח אחריו בן גדול הנודע בשם ר' יהודה כברכות ט:.
and he left behind a great son known by the name of R' Yehuda, as in Berakhot 9b.

div.head: Shimon b. Kimḥit.
div.ab: ‫ אמו קמחית היו לה שבעה בנים וכולן שמשו בכה״ג, ויסופר בירושלמי יומא פ״א ה״א״ד: ומובא גם ויק״ר פ״ך־יב, במ״ר פ״ב־כו שפ״א יצא שמעון בן קמחית (שהיה אז כה״ג) לדבר עם מלך הערבים וניתזא צינורא מפיו על בגדיו וטמאתו וגבגס יהודה אחיו ושימש תחתיו בכה״ג ואותו היום ראתה אמם שני בניה כה״ג.

His mother Kimḥit had seven sons, and all of them served in the High Priesthood. It is related in Yerushalmi Yoma 1:1 (4b), and also brought in Vayikra Rabbah 20:12, Bemidbar Rabbah 2:26, that one time Shimon b. Kimḥit (who was then High Priest) went out to speak with the king of the Arabs, and a spurt of saliva sprayed from his mouth onto his garments and rendered him impure; and his brother Yehuda entered and served in his stead in the High Priesthood, and on that day their mother saw two of her sons [as] High Priests.
ודעת החכם גרץ ח״ב צד ‪22‬י‪17‬‬ שהוא הנקרא בשם שמעון הצדיק, ונקל מאוד לכותב דה״י לתאר פלוני ופלוני בשם צדיק, אבל לחז״ל כבד מאוד הדבר, ואנו אין לנו אך שמעון הצדיק שהיה בזמן אלכסנדר מקרון.

And the opinion of the scholar Graetz, Volume 2, page 227 [perhaps 22, 17], is that he is the one called by the name Shimon ha-Tzaddik; and it is very easy for a writer of history to describe so-and-so by the title "Tzaddik" [the Righteous], but for our Sages of blessed memory the matter is very weighty, and we have only Shimon ha-Tzaddik who lived in the time of Alexander of Macedon [the Hebrew has "Makron", a printer's error for "Makedon"].

div.head: R' Shimon ben Shakfa.
div.ab: נזכר קה״ר פ״א רפ״יא ר׳ יודן בשמו.

This great Amora, although he did not merit to be the head of an academy, was nevertheless among the greatest disciples of Rav Huna and disseminated much Torah, and all the great Amoraim of the fourth generation were his disciples.
Of his family and his father's house nothing is known to us, though as it appears, his father was not a Torah scholar, as is proven in Avodah Zarah 50b, where Rav Sheshet said: "I am neither a carpenter [scholar] nor the son of a carpenter, etc." About himself he spoke by way of humility, but how could he say so about his father? From this it is implied that his father was not a Torah scholar.
His mother is mentioned in Bava Batra 9b, where Rav Sheshet became angry at Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami and felt distressed; Rav Aḥadvoi bar Ami became mute and forgot his learning. His mother (of Rav Sheshet) came and wept before him. She cried out and cried out, and he paid no attention to her. She said to him: "Look at these breasts from which you nursed!" He prayed for mercy for him and he was healed. This is according to the commentary of Rashi; however, the opinion of Tosafot there is that the mother of Rav Aḥadvoi had been the wet-nurse of Rav Sheshet, and she came before him so that he would pray for her son. And justice is with them, for

And the halakhot of Rav were so precious to him that when a halakhah was stated before him in the name of Rav and it did not seem right in his eyes, he would always say: "Rav stated this teaching when he was drowsy and lying down to sleep," as in Yevamot 24b, 91a, 109b, because he did not believe that it had issued from the mouth of Rav.
And when Rav Huna sat upon the chair of Rav in Sura, Rav Sheshet sat before him, as in Ketubot 69a: when Rav Anan sent to Rav Huna and called him "Huna our colleague," Rav Sheshet was sitting before him. Rav Huna said to him, "Go say to him—and let him who does not say it to him be under the ban..." Rav Sheshet went before Rav Anan and said to him, "The Master is a teacher, and Rav Huna is the teacher of the teacher, etc."
And likewise in Bava Batra 85b, Rav Sheshet inquired of Rav Huna.
And in Yevamot 62b they said that Rav Sheshet became sterile from the lectures of Rav Huna.
And in Zevaḥim 5b: Rav Huna and Rav Naḥman were sitting, and Rav Sheshet was sitting beside them.
וכן מצינו רב ששת אר״ה כב״מ עב:, עירובין פ״ג ה״ב.

And as for what we find in Pesaḥim 102b, "Rav Huna said that Rav Sheshet said," one must read "Rav Huna bar Yehudah" (who was a disciple of Rav Sheshet), in accordance with the reading of the Rif; and so too one must read in Menaḥot 39a.
And in Yoma 43b, Rav Sheshet recited his lecture and said to R' Yitzḥak, "Rav Huna has already interpreted your teaching in Babylonia."
And likewise we find: Rav Sheshet said that Rav Assi said, in Sanhedrin 33a and Ḥullin 92b.
Rav Sheshet said that R' Elazar said, in Yevamot 4a.
Rav Sheshet in the name of R' Elazar ben Azaryah, in Eruvin 64b and Pesaḥim 118a.
In the name of R' Ḥiyya, in Yerushalmi Eruvin 3:2.
Rav Sheshet said that R' Yoḥanan said, in Shabbat 37b.
And his diligence in Torah was so great that they said in Berakhot 8a that even at the time of prayer he would turn his face away and study.
And in Pesaḥim 68b they said that every thirty days he would review his learning, and he would lean and stand at the bolt of the door and say: "Rejoice, O my soul! Rejoice, O my soul! For you I have read Scripture, for you I have studied Mishnah."
And I heard from the mouth of my friend, the wise Rabbi, the genius of preachers, Rabbi Ḥayyim Zundel Maccoby, may his light shine, a fine and acceptable explanation: namely, because Rav Sheshet was blind, as is known, and a blind person is exempt from the commandments [according to one opinion], and nevertheless he toiled so much in the Torah—this was truly only for its own sake, without expectation of reward. And this is what he said: "Rejoice, O my soul! For you I have read Scripture, for you I have studied Mishnah"—that his study of Torah was solely and exclusively for his soul, without expectation of reward or ulterior motive.
And he rose so high in his expertise in Mishnayot and Baraitot that they said in Eruvin 67a that Rav Ḥisda's lips would tremble before the Baraitot of Rav Sheshet. And the colleagues of Rav Huna his teacher also knew that he was like "Sinai" [an encyclopedic scholar], as attested by Rav Naḥman in Shevuot 41b, who said: "It is I and Rav Sheshet who have learned halakhot, Sifra, Sifrei, Tosefta, and the entire Gemara."
And even regarding the great man of the generation, Rav Yehudah, they said in Yevamot 11b that when he inquired of Rav Sheshet (in the manner of colleagues), he immediately brought him resolutions from a Mishnah [or Baraita]. And when a Baraita was difficult for Rav Assi bar Natan, he went to Rav Sheshet to explain it, as in Nedarim 78a. And likewise they said in Avodah Zarah 42b: "Rav Sheshet collected the strict rulings of the Baraitot and taught them."
And in Zevaḥim 96b it is recounted that Rav Yitzḥak the son of Rav Yehudah was accustomed to study before Rami bar Ḥama; he left him and went to Rav Sheshet. One day

Rav Ḥisda: in Eruvin 67a they said that when they met one another, Rav Ḥisda's lips would tremble from the Baraitot of Rav Sheshet, and Rav Sheshet's entire body would tremble from the sharp analysis of Rav Ḥisda. And in Gittin 68a [see Ketubot 68a], when Rav Ḥisda and Rav Sheshet met one another, Rav Ḥisda prayed a prayer before him. Rav Sheshet asked his attendant what Rav Ḥisda was doing, and he told him that he was standing and praying; he said to his attendant, "Set me up as well, that I may pray: 'If this wretch is pushed aside, before whom is he pushed aside?'" He said to him, "Leave him be." And at that time he was already blind, and therefore he called himself "a wretch."
And likewise in Nedarim 78a: Rav Assi bar Natan found this Baraita difficult; he came to Nehardea before Rav Sheshet and did not find him; he came after him to Maḥoza and said to him, etc.
And how he became blind is explained in the commentary of Rabbenu Gershom at the end of Menaḥot, and it is likewise brought in the Responsa of the Geonim, Shaarei Teshuvah, section 178: that Rav would not lift his eyes from the ground, and Rav Yosef and Rav Sheshet wished to conduct themselves thus, and they became blind.
And likewise it is explicit in Berakhot 58a: Rav Sheshet was blind. Everyone was going to greet the face of the king, and Rav Sheshet arose and went with them. A certain Sadducee found him and said to him: "Whole pitchers go to the river; where do the broken shards go?" He said to him: "Come and see that I know more than you." ... The third troop passed by; when it was silent, Rav Sheshet said to him: "Certainly now the king is coming." ... Rav Sheshet opened his mouth and blessed him, etc.
And likewise in Shabbat 109a, where Rav Sheshet said: "Rocket-herb is beneficial even for me" (even though I am blind in the eyes, it is beneficial for me—Rashi); and so too it is explicit in Pesaḥim 116b.
However, this matter is clear: that he was not blind from birth and from the womb, as in Berakhot 57b, where they said that Rav Sheshet saw a snake in his dream and killed it.
And likewise in Bava Batra 9b, where his mother said to him: "Look at these breasts from which you nursed."
And behold, even though he disseminated Torah to a great multitude of disciples, and a Tanna [reciter of Baraitot] also sat before him and recited before him, as in Berakhot 37a, Sanhedrin 86a, and Horayot 9a, nevertheless he was not appointed as a judge, as in Ketubot 94b, where Rav Naḥman said to him: "First, I am a judge and the Master is not a judge"—and this was possibly because he was blind.

And with Rav Naḥman he was like a complete colleague and disputes with him throughout the entire Talmud, as in Berakhot 41b, etc., as is proven in the entry for Rav Naḥman; and in Ketubot 94b, when Rav Sheshet ruled on the law not in accordance with Rav Naḥman, Rav Naḥman said to him: "First, I am a judge (appointed by the Exilarch and the yeshiva, Rashi) and the Master is not a judge." Rabbah: even though we find in Kiddushin 53b "Rabbah said [in the name of] Rav Sheshet," nevertheless they were like colleagues, as in Eruvin 65a, though Rav Sheshet was without doubt older than him. Rabbah bar Shmuel: Rav Sheshet found Rabbah bar Shmuel [and] said to him: "Has the Master learned anything regarding the form of a doorway?" [in] Eruvin 11b; regarding sanctifications [in] Eruvin 39b; regarding a hired laborer [in] Shevuot 45b. Now, when Rav Huna passed away, the elder Rav Ḥisda sat in his place in Sura, as he was then eighty-two years old, and in the place of Rav Yehudah in Pumbedita reigned the young Rabbah his student, while Rav Sheshet disseminated Torah in Shilḥi, as is explicit in the Iggeret of Rav Sherira Gaon, part 3, chapter 2, and as appears from his words. His students and those who reported his statements: Nehardea, Shekhantziv, Shilḥi, and Meḥoza were towns close to one another, and this is what we find in Megillah 29a: "Rav Sheshet was sitting in the synagogue of Shaf ve-Yativ in Nehardea. The Divine Presence came and he did not go out; the ministering angels came and were frightening him. He said before Him: Master of the Universe, if someone is afflicted and someone is not afflicted, who [gives way before whom?]" R' Abba bar Kohen in his name in Yerushalmi Shabbat 6:1. R' Abbahu said [in the name of] Rav Sheshet in Keritot 22a. R' Anina inquired of Rav Sheshet in Ketubot 43a, and so one must read in Bekhorot 15a.

Rav Adda bar Ḥama said [in the name of] Rav Sheshet in Bava Metzia 30a. Rav Aḥa the son of Rav Huna said [in the name of] Rav Sheshet in Berakhot 32a, Eruvin 65b; he inquired of him [in] Bava Batra 70a, Sanhedrin 43a, 82b. Rav Aḥadboi bar Ami inquired of Rav Sheshet — he said to him: "You annoy us" in Sanhedrin 55a; and likewise the incident of Bava Batra 8a brought above; he said [in the name of] Rav Sheshet in Niddah 37b. Rav Idi his attendant (his servant, Rashi) heard a halakhah from him and went to the study hall and did not say it in his name, and Rav Sheshet cursed him in Bekhorot 31b. Rav Assi bar Natan found this baraita difficult [and] came before Rav Sheshet in Nedarim 78a. Rav Gadda heard him in Eruvin 11b. Rav Huna bar Ḥinena inquired of Rav Sheshet in Kiddushin 20b three times. Rav Huna bar Yehudah said [in the name of] Rav Sheshet in Eruvin 24b, 89a, Yoma 25a, Ketubot 63b, 100b, Bava Metzia 53b, Menaḥot 39b; and in Pesaḥim 102b "Rav Huna said [in the name of] Rav Sheshet," the words "bar Yehudah" are missing; and likewise Eruvin 26a, Yoma 70a "Rav Huna the son of Rav Yehoshua said [in the name of] Rav Sheshet," one must read "Rav Huna bar Yehudah" according to the version of the Rif and the Rosh; and in Shabbat 24a: "Rav Huna bar Yehudah happened to come to the house of Rava; he thought to recite 'Who builds Jerusalem.' Rav Sheshet said to him," etc. Rav Hamnuna objected to Rav Sheshet in Sanhedrin 33a, and Rav Sheshet called him "Hamnuna" in Eruvin 67a. R' Zeira inquired of Rav Sheshet in Sanhedrin 33b, Horayot 11a, Ḥullin 121a; and Rav Sheshet called him "a great man" in Eruvin 66a.

פרנסתו ומדותיו היקרות‬ ‫ומקראיו הפרטים‪.‬‬ ‫ הוא לא עשה את התורה קרדום לחפור בה ואך היה סוחר בבגדים שהיה נותנן בהקפה בגיטין יד: שאמרו רב ששת הוה ליה אשרתא דסרבלי במחוזא (שנתן סרבלים באשראי לתת לו‬ המעות לזמן קבוע, רש״י), א״ל לרב יוסף בר חמא בהדי דאתית אייתינהו ניהלי.

His livelihood, his precious character traits, and his personal incidents. He did not make the Torah a spade with which to dig, Rather, he was a merchant in garments which he would give on credit, [as] in Gittin 14b where they said: "Rav Sheshet had a credit of cloaks in Meḥoza (that he gave cloaks on credit, to give him the money at a fixed time, Rashi). He said to Rav Yosef bar Ḥama: When you come, bring them to me."
וה׳ בירך מעשי ידיו והיה עשיר כדמוכח נדה מז. שהיה לו שפחות, והיה מוסרן ‫לערבים כדי שלא יזונו בבנות ישראל.

And the Lord blessed the work of his hands and he was wealthy, as is proven [in] Niddah 47a, that he had maidservants, and he would hand them over to Arabs so that they would not commit prostitution with the daughters of Israel [?].
והיה איסתניס גדול כפסחים קח. דאי טעום מידי בצפרא, לאורתא לא הוה מהני ליה מיכלא ולכן היה מתענה ערב פסח כדי שיכול לאכול מצה בערב.

And he was a very delicate person, as in Pesaḥim 108a, that if he tasted anything in the morning, in the evening food would not benefit him, and therefore he would fast on the eve of Passover so that he would be able to eat matzah in the evening.

‫חיה והביאו‪ ,‬אז הוציא רב ששת הרגל‬ ‫ששמשיה לקח והגיחה אייל האס הבהמה‬ ‫בעלת חמש רגלים היא! אז א״ל הדיש‬ ‫גלותא שיעשו קמיה )ששמשו יראה שהכל‬ ‫נעשה בהכשר( אמר לו לחי‪ '/‬קריבו תבא‬ ‫קמייהו ואייתו קמיה בישרא ואותיבו קמיה‬ ‫ריםתגא דחגקא חמתא )וסברו יען שהיא‬ ‫עוד לא ירגיש ויחנק( גששיה ושקליה‬ ‫כרכה כםודריה לבתר דאכיל )ורצו לידע‬ ‫מה כריך בסודריה( א״ל איגגיב לן כסא‬ ‫דכםפא בהדי דקא מעייגי אשכחיה שבשר‬ ‫כרוך בסודריה א״ל שעשית זאת אך‬ ‫לצערן אמר להם לא‪ ,‬אך לכן לא אכלתי‬ ‫הבשר יען שהבהמה היתת בעלת שחין‬ ‫ומצאו כדבריו‪ ,‬כי קא גפיק ברו בירא‬ ‫ושדו ליד! ציפתא עילויה וסברו שהוא‬ ‫ילך על אותו מקום ויפיל לבור אך רב‬ ‫רב חסרא גחר ליה מאחוריה‪ ,‬א״ל רב‬ ‫ששת ליגוקא פסוק לי פסוקך א״ל גטה‬ ‫לך על יטיגך וכוי — א״ל רב חסדא‬ ‫מגא ידע טר‪ ,‬א׳׳ל חרא דגהר לי מד‬ ‫ועוד פסק לי יגוקא פסוקא ועוד דחשידי‬ ‫עבדי דלא מעלו‪.‬‬

Then Rav Sheshet took out the leg that his attendant had taken and placed it down, [and] said to him: "Is the animal five-legged?!" Then the Exilarch said to them that they should prepare [food] before him (so that his attendant would see that everything was done kosher). He said to them: "So be it." They brought a table before them and brought meat before him, and placed before him a piece that chokes the animal [?] (and they thought that because he was blind he would not feel it and would choke). He felt it and took it, [and] wrapped it in his kerchief. After he ate (and they wanted to know what was wrapped in his kerchief), they said to him: "A silver cup has been stolen from us." While they were searching, they found it—that meat was wrapped in his kerchief. They said to them [to the Exilarch] that he did this only to distress them. He said to them: "No, rather this is why I did not eat the meat, because the animal had boils," and they found it to be as he said. When he was going out, they dug a pit and threw a mat over it, and they thought that he would walk over that place and fall into the pit, but Rav Ḥisda snorted at him from behind him. Rav Sheshet said to a child: "Recite your verse for me." He said to him: "Turn yourself to your right," etc. — Rav Ḥisda said to him: "How did the Master know?" He said to him: "First, because the Master snorted at me; and furthermore, the child recited a verse for me; and furthermore, because the servants are suspected of not being virtuous."
